# Conditional VAE Architecture Overview



This page is the architectural entry point for DeSCOPE's deep-dive catalog: it explains how perturbation response prediction is framed as **conditional variational inference** and maps the four neural modules that implement it. Everything here is grounded in the two files that define the model family — `modeling_descope.py` (architecture and forward logic) and `configuration_descope.py` (dimensions and depths). Deeper treatments of each subsystem are deferred to their dedicated pages, linked at the end of each section.

## DeSCOPE in One View: A cVAE for Perturbation Response

DeSCOPE treats "predict how a cell responds to a perturbation" as a **conditional generative problem**: given a control cell profile and an embedding of the perturbed gene, the model generates the perturbed cell profile. The generative backbone is a conditional Variational Autoencoder (cVAE) in which the perturbed gene is represented by an **ESM2-derived protein embedding** rather than a learned token lookup. This design is stated directly in the project README and is visible in the canonical architecture figure below.

![DeSCOPE main architecture](https://github.com/Peg-Wu/DeSCOPE/blob/main/assets/main.png?raw=true)

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L20-L26), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L16-L17)

## Architectural Map

All model code lives in a compact `src/descope/models` package with a strict separation of concerns: configuration, network definitions, model assembly, and shared utilities (MLP builder, KL function, output dataclasses). The public classes `DeSCOPEForATAC` and `DeSCOPEForRNA` are re-exported at the package root, alongside `DeSCOPEConfig`.

```
src/descope/
├── models/
│   ├── baselines.py            # mean_baseline fallback model
│   ├── configuration_descope.py  # DeSCOPEConfig (dims, depths, activations)
│   ├── modeling_descope.py     # PertGeneEncoder, VariationalEncoder, VariationalDecoder,
│   │                           #   DeSCOPEForATAC, DeSCOPEForRNA
│   └── utils.py                # build_mlp, kl_loss_func, output dataclasses
├── __init__.py                 # exports DeSCOPEConfig, DeSCOPEForATAC, DeSCOPEForRNA, ...
└── trainer.py / inference.py   # consume the models (see Training / Inference pages)
```

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L1-L12), [__init__.py](/src/descope/__init__.py#L12-L14)

The full graph is small — four module types, wired once per modality. The diagram below shows the wiring with default dimensions from `DeSCOPEConfig` (`hidden_size=672`, `input_pert_gene_embedding_size=5120`, `input_length=18080`).

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    PE["Perturbation gene embedding (ESM2)<br/>5120-d"] --> PGE["PertGeneEncoder<br/>MLP 5120 → 672 (1 layer)"]
    PGE --> EMB["Perturbation embedding<br/>672-d"]

    CTRL["Control cell profile<br/>18080-d"] --> CP["concat → 18752"]
    EMB --> CP
    CP --> PRIOR["Prior Encoder<br/>MLP → (μ_p, logσ²_p), 4 layers"]

    LBL["Perturbed profile (labels)<br/>18080-d"] --> CL["concat → 18752"]
    EMB --> CL
    CL --> POST["Posterior Encoder<br/>MLP → (μ_q, logσ²_q, z_q), 4 layers"]

    POST --> REP["Reparameterization<br/>z = μ_q + ε·exp(0.5·logσ²_q)"]
    REP --> CD["concat → 1344"]
    EMB --> CD
    CD --> DEC["Decoder<br/>MLP 1344 → 18080 (4 layers)"]
    DEC --> SP["Softplus"]
    SP --> OUT["Predicted perturbed profile"]
```

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L119-L136), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L6-L20)

## Conditioning: One Embedding, Three Concatenation Points

The "C" in cVAE is implemented with a deliberately minimal pattern: the perturbation embedding is projected once and then **concatenated at every stage** of the generative pipeline. In each `forward` pass, the projected embedding is fused (i) with the control profile into the prior encoder, (ii) with the ground-truth perturbed labels into the posterior encoder, and (iii) with the latent sample `z` into the decoder. The perturbation thus acts as a **shared conditioning backbone** threading through prior, posterior, and reconstruction.

> [!TIP]
> Because the same projected embedding (`pert_embeddings`, 672-d) is reused in all three concatenations, the perturbation signal is the only feature shared across the prior, posterior, and decoder — this is what lets the prior alone (used at inference) generalize to unseen perturbations whose ESM2 embeddings differ from training genes.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L145-L152), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L231-L238)

## Core Building Blocks

Every trainable module is an MLP built by a single factory, `build_mlp`, which applies the pattern `Linear → LayerNorm (optional) → activation → Dropout` and omits activation/LayerNorm on the final projection layer. This keeps depth, width, dropout, and activation uniformly controlled by `DeSCOPEConfig`. The defaults define the canonical shapes: 672-d hidden state, 1-layer perturbation projector, 4-layer variational encoders, 4-layer decoder, GELU activations.

| Module | Class | Input → Output | Default depth | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Perturbation projector | `PertGeneEncoder` | 5120 → 672 | 1 | Projects ESM2 gene embedding into model space |
| Prior encoder | `VariationalEncoder(in_dim=input_length+672)` | 18752 → 672×2 | 4 | Outputs `(μ_p, logσ²_p)` of the prior Gaussian |
| Posterior encoder | `VariationalEncoder(in_dim=input_length+672)` | 18752 → 672×2 | 4 | Outputs `(μ_q, logσ²_q)` and sampled `z_q` |
| Decoder | `VariationalDecoder(in_dim=hidden_size*2)` | 1344 → 18080 | 4 | Reconstructs the full perturbed profile |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L15-L98), [utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L103-L111), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L5-L20)

The `VariationalEncoder` does something subtle with its single MLP: the network emits `hidden_size * 2` values, and `torch.chunk(..., 2, dim=-1)` splits the output into mean and log-variance halves — no separate heads are used. The reparameterization trick is then applied inline (`std = exp(0.5·logvar)`, `z = mean + ε·std`), making the latent sample differentiable w.r.t. the encoder parameters.

> [!TIP]
> Model assembly follows the HuggingFace convention: both top-level models subclass `DeSCOPEPretrainedModel`, which binds `config_class = DeSCOPEConfig`, then call `self.post_init()`. This means the full cVAE is a standard `PreTrainedModel` — it can be saved, reloaded with `from_pretrained`, and configured entirely through `DeSCOPEConfig` kwargs.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L67-L73), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L55-L58), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L101-L102)

## Dual-Path Data Flow: Training vs Inference

The architecture has two deliberately different execution paths. **Training** uses the posterior path: the ground-truth perturbed profile (`labels`) is fed to the posterior encoder alongside the perturbation embedding, producing `z_q` for reconstruction — the classic VAE setup where the approximate posterior sees the data. **Inference** uses the prior path only: `inference()` is decorated with `@torch.no_grad()`, samples `z` from the prior (conditioned on control profile + perturbation), and never touches `labels`. The two paths share the same perturbation embedding, decoder, and softplus output stage.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph TRAIN["Training (forward)"]
        L["labels"] --> QE["Posterior Encoder"] --> ZQ["z_q"] --> D["Decoder"]
        QE --> KL["KL(q‖p) term"]
        D --> SP["Softplus"] --> MSE["MSE term"]
    end
    subgraph INFER["Inference (inference)"]
        C2["control profile"] --> PE2["Prior Encoder"] --> ZP["z_p ~ prior"] --> D2["Decoder"]
        D2 --> SP2["Softplus"] --> P["Prediction"]
    end
    KL -. "closes the gap<br/>q → p" .-> PE2
```

| Aspect | `forward()` (training) | `inference()` (deployment) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latent source | Posterior: `[labels ‖ pert_emb]` | Prior: `[ctrl_profile ‖ pert_emb]` |
| Uses ground-truth labels | Yes | No (`@torch.no_grad()`) |
| Decoder input | `[z_q ‖ pert_emb]` | `[z_p ‖ pert_emb]` |
| Returns | `loss`, `mse_loss`, `kl_loss`, `logits` | `logits` only (losses = `None`) |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L138-L176), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L178-L196)

## ELBO Objective at a Glance

Both top-level models optimize a weighted ELBO: `loss = alpha_mse_loss × MSE + alpha_kl_loss × KL`, with both weights defaulting to `1.0` and settable at construction time. The MSE term compares softplus-activated predictions against labels and supports an optional per-feature `mse_weights` tensor for weighted supervision. The KL term closes the gap between the posterior and the conditioned prior; it is computed under `torch.amp.autocast(enabled=False)` with explicit `.float()` casts — the prior log-variance sits in a denominator, so this is done in float32 for numerical stability under mixed-precision training. The full loss composition, weighting strategy, and per-modality differences are covered in [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition).

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L155-L169), [utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L28-L41)

## Output Contract

Both models return HuggingFace `ModelOutput` dataclasses rather than bare tensors, giving downstream trainer and inference code a uniform interface: a total `loss`, its `mse_loss` and `kl_loss` components for logging, and `logits` holding the predicted (softplus-activated) profile.

| Field | Type | Training | Inference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loss` | scalar or `None` | Weighted ELBO total | `None` |
| `mse_loss` | scalar or `None` | Reconstruction MSE | `None` |
| `kl_loss` | scalar or `None` | KL(q‖p), batch-mean | `None` |
| `logits` | `(batch, input_length)` | Predictions | Predictions |

Sources: [utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L12-L25)

## RNA and ATAC: Two Classes, One Blueprint

The repository maintains `DeSCOPEForRNA` and `DeSCOPEForATAC` as **two structurally identical classes** — the source notes this explicitly: identical architectures, kept separate to allow independent per-modality adjustment. The only architectural divergence is the perturbation projector: ATAC uses the configurable `PertGeneEncoder` (built via `build_mlp`), while RNA uses a hard-coded `Linear → LayerNorm` pair. Input tensor names also differ semantically (`ctrl_cell_expr` for RNA transcript expression, `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` for ATAC TF-IDF profiles), but their shapes and roles are identical. Full details live in [RNA and ATAC Model Variants](11-rna-and-atac-model-variants).

| Aspect | `DeSCOPEForRNA` | `DeSCOPEForATAC` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Perturbation projector | `nn.Sequential(Linear, LayerNorm)` | `PertGeneEncoder` (configurable MLP) |
| Control input name | `ctrl_cell_expr` | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` |
| Encoder/prior/decoder wiring | Identical | Identical |
| Loss & output contract | `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` | `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L118), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L209-L213), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L127)

This page established the skeleton. The catalog decomposes it along four axes — follow them in this order for a complete mental model:

1. **Component deep dives**: [PertGene Encoder and ESM2 Embeddings](8-pertgene-encoder-and-esm2-embeddings) → [Prior and Posterior Variational Encoders](9-prior-and-posterior-variational-encoders) → [Decoder and Softplus Output Design](10-decoder-and-softplus-output-design)
2. **Configuration surface**: every dimension and depth referenced above maps to a config field — see [Model Configuration Reference](7-model-configuration-reference)
3. **Objective**: how the two loss terms interact in practice — [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition)
4. **Lifecycle**: how these models are driven end-to-end — [Trainer and Accelerate Integration](15-trainer-and-accelerate-integration) and [Inference Pipeline Design](19-inference-pipeline-design)

# Model Configuration Reference



This page is the complete reference for every configuration surface in DeSCOPE: the three CLI argument dataclasses in `arguments.py`, the serializable `DeSCOPEConfig`, the DeSCOPE-specific training fields, and how all of them flow into `DeSCOPEForRNA` / `DeSCOPEForATAC`. It covers defaults, types, CLI syntax, and the checkpoint/reload contract. For architectural behavior of the components these knobs control, see [Conditional VAE Architecture Overview](6-conditional-vae-architecture-overview).

## Configuration Architecture: From CLI to Model

DeSCOPE uses a three-tier configuration contract. Tier 1 is the command line, parsed by HuggingFace's `HfArgumentParser` into three orthogonal dataclasses. Tier 2 is `DeSCOPEConfig`, a `PretrainedConfig` subclass that captures the architecture and is JSON-serializable. Tier 3 is the model constructor, where loss weights are injected directly rather than through config.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph CLI["Tier 1: Command Line"]
        MP["MODELPARAMS<br/>--hidden_size=672 ..."]
        DP["DATAPARAMS<br/>--ctrl_name, --gene_embs_file"]
        TP["TRAINPARAMS<br/>--alpha_mse_loss, --learning_rate ..."]
    end
    subgraph ARGS["Tier 2: Dataclasses (arguments.py)"]
        MA["DeSCOPEModelArguments"]
        DA["DeSCOPEDataArguments"]
        TA["DeSCOPETrainingArguments"]
    end
    subgraph CORE["Tier 3: Model Core"]
        CFG["DeSCOPEConfig<br/>(PretrainedConfig, model_type='descope')"]
        M["DeSCOPEForRNA / DeSCOPEForATAC<br/>alpha_mse_loss, alpha_kl_loss"]
        TR["DeSCOPETrainer"]
    end
    DS["HFDatasetForRNA / HFDatasetForATAC"]
    MP --> MA -->|"7 architecture fields"| CFG
    DP --> DA --> DS
    TP --> TA
    TA -->|"loss weights only"| M
    TA --> TR
    DS -->|"input_length & embedding size inferred<br/>from first sample"| CFG
    CFG --> M
```

Every training entrypoint — `tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py`, `tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train.py`, and the Tahoe-100M pretraining script — parses the identical triple `(DeSCOPEDataArguments, DeSCOPEModelArguments, DeSCOPETrainingArguments)` via `parser.parse_args_into_dataclasses()`, so the configuration surface is stable across all pipelines.

Sources: [arguments.py](/src/descope/arguments.py#L1-L85), [train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L18-L22), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28)

## DeSCOPEModelArguments

`DeSCOPEModelArguments` is the CLI-exposed architecture surface. All seven fields map one-to-one onto `DeSCOPEConfig` attributes and ultimately parameterize the MLPs built by `build_mlp`.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI flag | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden_act` | `str` | `"gelu"` | `--hidden_act` | Activation lookup via `ACT2FN[config.hidden_act]` in every `build_mlp` call |
| `hidden_size` | `int` | `672` | `--hidden_size` | Width of all hidden layers; also defines latent dimension |
| `hidden_dropout` | `float` | `0` | `--hidden_dropout` | `nn.Dropout` inside each hidden block |
| `pert_gene_encoder_layers` | `int` | `1` | `--pert_gene_encoder_layers` | `PertGeneEncoder` MLP depth (see RNA/ATAC note below) |
| `variational_encoder_layers` | `int` | `4` | `--variational_encoder_layers` | Prior and posterior encoder depth |
| `variational_decoder_layers` | `int` | `4` | `--variational_decoder_layers` | Decoder depth |
| `add_layernorm` | `bool` | `True` | `--add_layernorm` | `nn.LayerNorm` after each `Linear` in `build_mlp` |

`hidden_size` is the highest-leverage field: it is not merely layer width. The variational encoder outputs `hidden_size * 2` values split into `mean` and `logvar` vectors, so the latent space `z` is `hidden_size`-dimensional, and the decoder input is `hidden_size * 2` (`z` concatenated with the perturbation embedding). Changing `hidden_size` therefore reshapes the latent bottleneck and decoder input simultaneously. The activation field accepts any key from `transformers.activations.ACT2FN` (`gelu`, `relu`, `silu`, `tanh`, ...), and `build_mlp` applies activation and dropout only to hidden blocks — the final projection layer is a bare `Linear` with no activation or dropout.

Sources: [arguments.py](/src/descope/arguments.py#L49-L85), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L36-L98), [models/utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L103-L142)

## DeSCOPEConfig: The Persistence Contract

`DeSCOPEConfig` is the serializable architecture record. It extends `transformers.PretrainedConfig`, registers `model_type = "descope"`, and is the class bound to all DeSCOPE models via `config_class = DeSCOPEConfig` on the `DeSCOPEPretrainedModel` base. This binding is what makes `save_pretrained` / `from_pretrained` round-trips restore the full architecture without re-specifying model arguments.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden_act` | `str` | `"gelu"` | Activation function for hidden layers |
| `hidden_size` | `int` | `672` | Hidden width; latent `z` is `hidden_size`-dim |
| `hidden_dropout` | `float` | `0` | Dropout rate in hidden blocks |
| `pert_gene_encoder_layers` | `int` | `1` | Perturbation gene encoder depth |
| `variational_encoder_layers` | `int` | `4` | Prior/posterior variational encoder depth |
| `variational_decoder_layers` | `int` | `4` | Decoder depth |
| `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` | `int` | `5120` | Input perturbation embedding width (matches ESM2); **inferred from data** |
| `input_length` | `int` | `18080` | Output dimension (number of genes/peaks); **inferred from data** |
| `add_layernorm` | `bool` | `True` | LayerNorm after hidden `Linear` layers |

The two `input_*` dimensions are the only config fields not exposed on `DeSCOPEModelArguments`; they are computed from the first training sample at model-construction time, as detailed in the next section. The defaults of `5120` and `18080` document the reference setup: ESM2-derived perturbation embeddings and the gene/peak vocabulary size used in the RNA and ATAC tutorials.

Sources: [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L101-L102)

## DeSCOPETrainingArguments

`DeSCOPETrainingArguments` extends the accelerate-style `TrainingArguments` from `wppkg.dl` and adds exactly three DeSCOPE-specific fields. Because it inherits the base class, every standard training knob (`seed`, `learning_rate`, `num_train_epochs`, `per_device_train_batch_size`, `gradient_accumulation_steps`, `max_grad_norm`, `lr_scheduler_type`, `weight_decay`, `num_warmup_ratio`, `mixed_precision`, `checkpointing_steps`, `resume_from_checkpoint`, dataloader options, and tracking options) is available on the CLI — all of these are exercised in the tutorial launch scripts.

| DeSCOPE field | Type | Default | CLI flag | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha_mse_loss` | `float` | `1.0` | `--alpha_mse_loss` | Weight of the reconstruction MSE term in `loss = α_mse · mse + α_kl · kl` |
| `alpha_kl_loss` | `float` | `1.0` | `--alpha_kl_loss` | Weight of the KL divergence term; see [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition) |
| `pretrained_model_name_or_path` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | `--pretrained_model_name_or_path` | When `None`, model trains from scratch with a fresh `DeSCOPEConfig`; otherwise loads via `from_pretrained` |

> [!TIP]
> The loss weights are stored directly on the model module (`self.alpha_mse_loss = alpha_mse_loss`), **not** inside `DeSCOPEConfig`. They therefore do not round-trip through `config.json`: when resuming with `--pretrained_model_name_or_path`, you must re-pass `alpha_mse_loss` and `alpha_kl_loss` on the command line, exactly as every tutorial script does in its `from_pretrained` branch. Omitting them silently reverts to the defaults of `1.0`.

Sources: [arguments.py](/src/descope/arguments.py#L6-L22), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L218-L219), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L169), [train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L71-L77)

## DeSCOPEDataArguments

`DeSCOPEDataArguments` points the model at its tokenized inputs. These fields configure `HFDatasetForRNA` / `HFDatasetForATAC` (see [Tokenization: AnnData to HuggingFace Datasets](12-tokenization-anndata-to-huggingface-datasets)), and two of them indirectly determine model dimensions.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI flag | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tokenized_datasets_dir` | `str` | `"./tokenized_dataset/K562"` | `--tokenized_datasets_dir` | Path to tokenized HF dataset(s); if the direct path is not a dataset, each subdirectory is loaded and concatenated |
| `keep_in_memory` | `bool` | `False` | `--keep_in_memory` | Materialize the dataset in RAM via `load_from_disk` |
| `ctrl_name` | `str` | `"control"` | `--ctrl_name` | Label identifying control cells in the tokenized dataset; **must match the tokenization-time naming** |
| `gene_embs_file` | `str` | `"./ESM2_pert_features.pt"` | `--gene_embs_file` | `.pt` file of perturbation embeddings; its width becomes `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` |

The defaults encode the reference K562 RNA pipeline, but the tutorials demonstrate that `ctrl_name` and `gene_embs_file` are dataset-specific: the K562 RNA tutorial uses `ctrl_name="non-targeting"`, the GM12878 ATAC tutorial uses `ctrl_name="control"`, and the Tahoe-100M drug pretraining uses `ctrl_name="DMSO_TF_0.0"` with drug-dose embeddings (`tahoe100m_drug_dose_embed.pt`) replacing the ESM2 gene embedding file. The embedding file's width flows directly into `input_pert_gene_embedding_size`, so swapping embedding sources (e.g., drug-dose vectors for gene-disease vectors) requires no config changes — the dimension is discovered at runtime.

Sources: [arguments.py](/src/descope/arguments.py#L25-L46), [train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L44-L49), [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train_descope.sh#L5-L7), [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train_descope.sh#L5-L7), [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/tahoe100m_pretrain/train_descope.sh#L5-L7)

## Data-Inferred Input Dimensions

The two structural dimensions — input perturbation embedding width and output vocabulary length — are deliberately excluded from the CLI and inferred from the first dataset sample in every entrypoint script:

```python
config = DeSCOPEConfig(
    input_pert_gene_embedding_size=train_ds[0]["pert_gene_emb"].shape[-1],
    input_length=train_ds[0]["labels"].shape[-1],
    ...
)
```

| Config field | Inferred from | Reference default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` | `train_ds[0]["pert_gene_emb"].shape[-1]` | `5120` (ESM2) | Width of perturbation representation input to the perturbation encoder |
| `input_length` | `train_ds[0]["labels"].shape[-1]` | `18080` | Output width of the decoder (genes for RNA, peaks for ATAC) |

This design means the same `MODELPARAMS` block works unchanged across the gene-perturbation tutorials (18,080-dim vocabularies), the Tahoe-100M pretraining (2k-HVG vocabulary), and any new tokenized dataset — the model always conforms to the data. The consequence for tuning is that `input_length` is only adjustable upstream, through tokenization and vocabulary selection (see [Feature Alignment and Vocabulary Handling](14-feature-alignment-and-vocabulary-handling)), never at training time.

Sources: [train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L54-L64), [train.py](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train.py#L54-L64), [3_train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/tahoe100m_pretrain/3_train.py#L58-L68), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L14-L15)

## Canonical Launch Configurations

The tutorial shell scripts are executable configuration references: `MODELPARAMS`, `DATAPARAMS`, and `TRAINPARAMS` blocks are assembled and forwarded to `accelerate launch`. The model-parameter block is byte-identical across all three published pipelines, confirming that `672`/`gelu`/`1-4-4` depths is the validated production configuration:

```bash
MODELPARAMS="
    --hidden_act=gelu \
    --hidden_size=672 \
    --hidden_dropout=0 \
    --pert_gene_encoder_layers=1 \
    --variational_encoder_layers=4 \
    --variational_decoder_layers=4 \
    --add_layernorm=True"
```

Where the pipelines diverge is exclusively in `TRAINPARAMS` and `DATAPARAMS` — scale-related training hyperparameters and dataset identity:

| Parameter | Gene tutorials (K562 / GM12878) | Tahoe-100M pretrain |
|---|---|---|
| `num_train_epochs` | `20` | `10` |
| `per_device_train_batch_size` | `64` | `256` |
| `gradient_accumulation_steps` | `1` | `1` |
| `learning_rate` | `1e-4` | `1e-4` |
| `lr_scheduler_type` | `cosine` | `cosine` |
| `num_warmup_ratio` | `0.1` | `0.05` |
| `logging_steps` | `50` | `200` |
| `checkpointing_steps` | `epoch-10` | `epoch-2` |
| `dataloader_num_workers` | `16` | `8` |
| `accelerate num_processes` | `1` | `4` |
| `ctrl_name` | `non-targeting` / `control` | `DMSO_TF_0.0` |
| `gene_embs_file` | `ESM2_pert_features.pt` | `tahoe100m_drug_dose_embed.pt` |
| `alpha_mse_loss` / `alpha_kl_loss` | `1.0` / `1.0` | `1.0` / `1.0` |

Note the two checkpointing formats supported by the trainer: integer steps (`--checkpointing_steps=500`) or the string form `epoch-N` meaning "every N epochs" (`epoch-10` in the gene tutorials, `epoch-2` in Tahoe pretraining).

Sources: [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train_descope.sh#L10-L59), [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train_descope.sh#L27-L58), [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/tahoe100m_pretrain/train_descope.sh#L27-L58), [trainer.py](/src/descope/trainer.py#L184-L197)

## RNA vs ATAC: Divergent Config Consumption

Both model classes accept the same `DeSCOPEConfig` and share identical variational encoder/decoder construction, but they consume the perturbation-encoder configuration differently. The source comments state the two architectures are kept as distinct classes to support independent adjustment per modality ([modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L118)).

| Config field | `DeSCOPEForRNA` | `DeSCOPEForATAC` |
|---|---|---|
| `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` | `nn.Linear` input width | `build_mlp` input width |
| `hidden_size` | `nn.Linear` output width | `build_mlp` output width |
| `pert_gene_encoder_layers` | **not consumed** — encoder is hardcoded as one `Linear` + `LayerNorm` | honored — depth of the `build_mlp` encoder |
| `hidden_act` / `hidden_dropout` / `add_layernorm` (pert encoder) | **not consumed** — `LayerNorm` always applied, no activation/dropout | honored — full `build_mlp` behavior |
| `variational_encoder_layers` | honored (prior + posterior) | honored (prior + posterior) |
| `variational_decoder_layers` | honored | honored |
| Forward signature | `ctrl_cell_expr` | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` |
| Output dataclass | `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` | `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` |

> [!TIP]
> If you increase `pert_gene_encoder_layers` or change `hidden_act`/`hidden_dropout` expecting an effect on the RNA pipeline, verify against the checkpoint's parameter shapes first: `DeSCOPEForRNA` constructs its perturbation encoder as `nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(emb_size, hidden_size), nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size))` regardless of those fields. Only the ATAC variant routes these values through `PertGeneEncoder`/`build_mlp`.

For component-level behavior of these submodules, see [PertGene Encoder and ESM2 Embeddings](8-pertgene-encoder-and-esm2-embeddings), [Prior and Posterior Variational Encoders](9-prior-and-posterior-variational-encoders), and the modality comparison in [RNA and ATAC Model Variants](11-rna-and-atac-model-variants).

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L15-L33), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L199-L222), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L208-L213)

## Checkpoint and Reload Semantics

The configuration lifecycle closes with the checkpoint contract. During training, the `DeSCOPETrainer` writes checkpoints to `output_dir/epoch_{i}/model` (or `step_{i}/model`) whenever `checkpointing_steps` triggers, and always persists the final model to `output_dir/last_model`. Because every DeSCOPE model carries `config_class = DeSCOPEConfig`, reloading through `from_pretrained` reconstructs the architecture from the serialized config — no `DeSCOPEConfig` or model-argument re-specification is needed at resume or fine-tune time.

The three-field reload checklist for `--pretrained_model_name_or_path` is therefore: (1) architecture — restored automatically from the checkpoint config; (2) loss weights — re-pass `alpha_mse_loss`/`alpha_kl_loss` explicitly; (3) data dims — nothing to do, since they live in the restored config and the new dataset must match them (mismatched vocabulary requires re-tokenization, not config overrides). Distributed/DeepSpeed checkpoint state is handled separately by the accelerate layer; see [Checkpointing, Resuming, Early Stopping](17-checkpointing-resuming-early-stopping) and [Distributed Training with DeepSpeed](18-distributed-training-with-deepspeed).

Sources: [trainer.py](/src/descope/trainer.py#L155-L161), [trainer.py](/src/descope/trainer.py#L184-L200), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L101-L102), [train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L71-L77)

- [PertGene Encoder and ESM2 Embeddings](8-pertgene-encoder-and-esm2-embeddings) — internals of the module governed by `pert_gene_encoder_layers`

- [Trainer and Accelerate Integration](15-trainer-and-accelerate-integration) — how `DeSCOPETrainingArguments` drives the training loop
- [API Reference and Module Layout](23-api-reference-and-module-layout) — module-level index of `descope.arguments` and `descope.models`

# PertGene Encoder and ESM2 Embeddings



The perturbation conditioning pathway is the only mechanism by which DeSCOPE learns *which* perturbation a cell is subjected to. This page documents the two components that implement it: the **ESM2 embedding supply chain** — precomputed protein-language-model vectors stored in `ESM2_pert_features.pt` and resolved at dataset load time — and the **`PertGeneEncoder`**, the neural head that projects a 5120-dimensional ESM2 vector into the 672-dimensional conditioning signal consumed by every branch of the conditional VAE. All claims below are traced to the implementation; where RNA and ATAC models diverge, the divergence is documented explicitly because it has direct configuration consequences.

## The Embedding Supply Chain: From ESM2 to Batch Tensor

DeSCOPE does **not** run ESM2 inside the training loop. Perturbation features are consumed as a precomputed PyTorch artifact — a dictionary file mapping gene symbols to embedding tensors, with the default path `./ESM2_pert_features.pt` hard-coded as a constructor default in every dataset class (`dataset.py` defaults it in `BaseDataset`, `DatasetForATAC`, `DatasetForRNA`, and `HFBaseDataset`). The `.pt` file maps `{gene_name: torch.Tensor}` and is loaded via `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` inside `load_gene_embs`.

At dataset construction time, the embedding dictionary is filtered to the perturbations actually present in the data: `BaseDataset` loads embeddings for the unique values of the perturbation column, while the fast `HFBaseDataset` requests `self.ds.unique("pert_gene")` from the Arrow-backed dataset. The stored HF dataset features are only `labels`, `pert_gene`, and `celltype` — the embedding itself is **injected at batch-assembly time** in `__getitems__`, where per-sample vectors are stacked into `batch["pert_gene_emb"]`. This design keeps embedding tensors out of the serialized dataset and lets you swap the `.pt` file without re-tokenizing.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["ESM2 protein language model<br/>(executed offline, outside this repo)"] -->|"per-gene vectors"| B["ESM2_pert_features.pt<br/>{gene: Tensor(5120)}"]
    B --> C["load_gene_embs()<br/>src/descope/utils.py"]
    C -->|"alias fix + zero-fill +<br/>multi-gene mean pooling"| D["gene_embs dict<br/>{perturbation: Tensor(5120)}"]
    D --> E["BaseDataset / HFBaseDataset"]
    F["HF Arrow dataset<br/>{labels, pert_gene, celltype}"] --> E
    E -->|"batch['pert_gene_emb'] (B, 5120)"| G["pert_gene_encoder"]
    G --> H["pert_embeddings (B, 672)<br/>conditioning vector"]
```

Sources: [dataset.py](/src/descope/dataset.py#L37-L71), [dataset.py](/src/descope/dataset.py#L190-L224), [utils.py](/src/descope/utils.py#L378-L404), [dataset.py](/src/descope/dataset.py#L277-L286)

> [!TIP]
> Because the repo ships no ESM2 inference script, `ESM2_pert_features.pt` is a first-class input artifact: if your perturbation set contains genes absent from the file, they will be silently replaced by zero vectors (with a log warning) — validate coverage before a long training run.

## Embedding Resolution Rules in `load_gene_embs`

`load_gene_embs` is the single normalization layer between the raw `.pt` dictionary and the model's expectations. It guarantees that every perturbation named in `perts_to_emb` receives a tensor, applying three deterministic fallback rules. First, a **gene alias** is patched: if `TAFAZZIN` exists but `TAZ` does not, the entry is duplicated under `TAZ`. Second, **multi-gene perturbations** — denoted by `+` in the perturbation label (e.g., `"GeneA+GeneB"`), a convention the tokenizer notebooks also enforce — are reduced by **mean pooling** over their constituent gene vectors, so a dual knockout occupies the same 5120-dimensional slot as a single knockout. Third, **missing genes become zero vectors**: an absent single-gene perturbation receives a zero tensor, and an absent gene inside a multi-gene combination contributes a zero vector to the mean. All three resolutions are reported through structured logging that distinguishes missing single-gene perturbations from multi-gene perturbations with partially missing constituents.

| Case in `perts_to_emb` | Resolution | Effect on conditioning signal |
|---|---|---|
| Gene present in `.pt` file | Returned as-is | Full ESM2 semantic content |
| `TAZ` (alias) | Copied from `TAFAZZIN` entry | Full content under alternate symbol |
| Multi-gene `"GeneA+GeneB"`, both present | Mean of the two 5120-d vectors | Joint perturbation represented in shared space |
| Multi-gene, one constituent missing | Mean includes a zero vector for the missing gene | Attenuated embedding, flagged in logs |
| Single gene missing entirely | Zero vector (5120-d) | No-op conditioning; model sees bias-like input |

Note that `BaseDataset.__getitem__` additionally casts each retrieved embedding with `.to(torch.float32)`, guarding against mixed-precision artifacts stored in the file.

Sources: [utils.py](/src/descope/utils.py#L404-L416), [utils.py](/src/descope/utils.py#L418-L450), [utils.py](/src/descope/utils.py#L390-L395), [dataset.py](/src/descope/dataset.py#L79-L99)

## The `PertGeneEncoder` Architecture

`PertGeneEncoder` is a thin wrapper around a feed-forward network constructed by the repository's generic `build_mlp` factory. Its contract is fixed by tensor shape: input `(batch_size, input_pert_gene_embedding_size)`, output `(batch_size, hidden_size)` — a compression from 5120 to 672 dimensions. The default configuration (`pert_gene_encoder_layers=1`) makes this a single linear projection followed by LayerNorm, because `build_mlp` treats depth 1 specially: a one-layer stack is `Linear → [LayerNorm]` with **no activation or dropout**, while deeper stacks follow the canonical `Linear → LayerNorm → activation → Dropout` block pattern repeated through hidden layers, terminated by a bare final `Linear` (no trailing normalization or activation). The final-layer asymmetry matters: the encoder's output is never non-negative or normalized unless `add_layernorm` semantics of the *last block* apply — which they do not for `n_layers > 1`.

| Config parameter | Default | Role in `PertGeneEncoder` |
|---|---|---|
| `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` | `5120` (`# ESM2: 5120`) | Input width; matches ESM2-15B's 5120-d hidden size |
| `hidden_size` | `672` | Output width; also the MLP hidden width for deeper stacks |
| `pert_gene_encoder_layers` | `1` | MLP depth (minimum 1, enforced) |
| `hidden_act` | `"gelu"` | Activation resolved via `ACT2FN` (layers ≥ 2 only) |
| `hidden_dropout` | `0` | Dropout rate (layers ≥ 2 only) |
| `add_layernorm` | `True` | LayerNorm after each `Linear` except the final one |

The 5120 default is annotated in `DeSCOPEConfig` with the comment `# ESM2: 5120`, consistent with the hidden width of the ESM2-15B checkpoint (`esm2_t48_15B_UR50D`). If you substitute a smaller ESM2 variant (e.g., 3B → 2560-d), you must override `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` in the config or the projection matrix will be shape-mismatched at model construction.

| `pert_gene_encoder_layers` | Constructed module composition |
|---|---|
| `1` (default) | `Linear(5120, 672) → LayerNorm(672)` |
| `2` | `Linear(5120, 672) → LayerNorm → GELU → Dropout → Linear(672, 672)` |
| `n ≥ 3` | First block + `(n−2)` × `[Linear(672, 672) → LayerNorm → GELU → Dropout]` + final `Linear(672, 672)` |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L15-L33), [utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L103-L142), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28)

> [!TIP]
> The RNA model does not actually instantiate `PertGeneEncoder`: the call is commented out and replaced by an inline `nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(5120, 672), nn.LayerNorm(672))` in `DeSCOPEForRNA.__init__`. Consequently, `pert_gene_encoder_layers` only takes effect for ATAC checkpoints unless you re-enable the class — a common source of confusion when porting configurations between modalities.

## RNA vs. ATAC: Two Conditioning Heads with One Interface

Both model classes satisfy the same interface — an attribute named `pert_gene_encoder` that maps `(B, 5120) → (B, 672)` — but their implementations differ. `DeSCOPEForATAC` uses the configurable `PertGeneEncoder` MLP; `DeSCOPEForRNA` uses a hard-coded `Linear + LayerNorm` pair. The source comments explain the design intent: the RNA and ATAC architectures are otherwise identical, and are deliberately maintained as two distinct model classes *to support independent adjustment for each data modality*. The divergent conditioning head is exactly that independent adjustment point — RNA embeddings evidently needed only a linear affine projection with normalization, while ATAC retains depth/activation flexibility.

| Aspect | `DeSCOPEForATAC` | `DeSCOPEForRNA` |
|---|---|---|
| Conditioning head | `PertGeneEncoder(config)` (configurable MLP) | Inline `nn.Sequential(Linear, LayerNorm)` |
| Honors `pert_gene_encoder_layers` / `hidden_act` / `hidden_dropout` | Yes | No (MLP instantiation commented out) |
| Input → output shape | `(B, 5120) → (B, 672)` | `(B, 5120) → (B, 672)` |
| Normalization | LayerNorm per `build_mlp` / `add_layernorm` | `LayerNorm(672)` always, appended to the linear map |
| Modality input name | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` | `ctrl_cell_expr` |

This split explains why checkpoint state dicts are not interchangeable across modalities even though every downstream module shape matches: the parameter names and layer structures under `pert_gene_encoder` differ.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L137), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L199-L216), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L209-L213)

## Conditioning Mechanics in the Forward Pass

The projected `pert_embeddings` tensor is the glue of the conditional VAE: the *same* conditioning vector is concatenated onto the input of **all three** generative branches. In `DeSCOPEForATAC.forward`, `pert_embeddings` is concatenated with the control-cell profile to form the prior encoder input, with the ground-truth target profile (`labels`) to form the posterior encoder input, and with the sampled latent `posterior_z` to form the decoder input. The identical pattern holds in `DeSCOPEForRNA.forward` (with `ctrl_cell_expr`) and in both `inference()` paths — inference differs only in sampling `z` from the prior instead of the posterior, while conditioning on `pert_embeddings` identically. This means the perturbation identity modulates not only what the model *predicts*, but where the latent distribution is centered and how it is decoded.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PGE["pert_gene_emb<br/>(B, 5120)"] --> ENC["pert_gene_encoder"]
    ENC --> PE["pert_embeddings<br/>(B, 672)"]
    CTRL["ctrl_cell_tf_idf / ctrl_cell_expr<br/>(B, 18080)"] --> C1(("concat"))
    PE --> C1 -->|"B, 18752"| PRIOR["prior_encoder"]
    LBL["labels<br/>(B, 18080)"] --> C2(("concat"))
    PE --> C2 -->|"B, 18752"| POST["posterior_encoder"]
    POST -->|"posterior_z (B, 672)"| C3(("concat"))
    PE --> C3 -->|"B, 1344"| DEC["decoder"]
    DEC --> SP["softplus"] --> OUT["preds<br/>(B, 18080)"]
```

The dimensional arithmetic follows directly from the config: encoders receive `input_length + hidden_size = 18080 + 672 = 18752`, and the decoder receives `hidden_size * 2 = 1344`. Note that the model is fully agnostic to ESM2 semantics downstream of the projection — from the VAE's perspective, `pert_gene_emb` is just a 5120-d real vector, so any alternative perturbation featurization of matching width (or zero vectors for missing entries, per the resolution rules above) flows through unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Data["Data layer"]
        DS["HFBaseDataset.__getitems__<br/>stacks gene_embs → pert_gene_emb"]
    end
    subgraph Model["Model layer"]
        CFG["DeSCOPEConfig<br/>input_pert_gene_embedding_size=5120<br/>hidden_size=672"]
        ENC["PertGeneEncoder<br/>(build_mlp)"]
        ATAC["DeSCOPEForATAC"]
        RNA["DeSCOPEForRNA"]
    end
    CFG -->|"dims"| ENC
    ENC -->|"instantiated by"| ATAC
    RNA -->|"bypasses: inline Linear+LayerNorm"| ATAC
    DS -->|"batch['pert_gene_emb']"| ATAC
    DS -->|"batch['pert_gene_emb']"| RNA
```

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L138-L176), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L224-L262), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L178-L196), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L264-L282), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L13-L27)

## Summary of Component Responsibilities

To close the loop: ESM2 embeddings enter DeSCOPE as a static dictionary artifact, are normalized by `load_gene_embs` (aliasing, mean pooling for `+`-combined perturbations, zero-vector fallbacks), and are attached to training batches by the dataset classes rather than stored in the serialized HF dataset. The `PertGeneEncoder` head then performs a single learned compression from the 5120-d protein-language space into the 672-d conditioning space, producing the tensor that conditions the prior, posterior, and decoder simultaneously. The two concrete consequences for advanced users are (1) embedding coverage is validated only through logs, so auditing `load_gene_embs` output against your perturbation list is a required pre-training step, and (2) head architecture is modality-dependent, with RNA fixed to a linear+LayerNorm projection regardless of encoder-depth configuration.

| Component | Module | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `ESM2_pert_features.pt` | External artifact | `{gene: Tensor(5120)}`, loaded with `weights_only=False` |
| `load_gene_embs` | `descope.utils` | Guarantees an entry per requested perturbation; zero-fill + mean-pool fallbacks |
| `HFBaseDataset` / `BaseDataset` | `descope.dataset` | Injects `pert_gene_emb` into each batch; float32 cast |
| `PertGeneEncoder` | `descope.models.modeling_descope` | `(B, 5120) → (B, 672)`; configurable via `build_mlp` |
| `DeSCOPEForATAC` / `DeSCOPEForRNA` | `descope.models.modeling_descope` | Consume `pert_embeddings` in prior, posterior, and decoder branches |

Sources: [utils.py](/src/descope/utils.py#L378-L464), [dataset.py](/src/descope/dataset.py#L277-L313), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L145-L153)

To continue through the core model components, proceed to [Prior and Posterior Variational Encoders](9-prior-and-posterior-variational-encoders) and [Decoder and Softplus Output Design](10-decoder-and-softplus-output-design), which detail the branches that consume `pert_embeddings`; [RNA and ATAC Model Variants](11-rna-and-atac-model-variants) expands on the modality split introduced above, and [Model Configuration Reference](7-model-configuration-reference) enumerates every knob summarized in the parameter table.

# Prior and Posterior Variational Encoders



DeSCOPE's generative core is a conditional VAE whose variational machinery is implemented in a single reusable class: `VariationalEncoder`. Two instances of this class — the **prior encoder** and the **posterior encoder** — parameterize two diagonal Gaussian distributions over the latent space, conditioned on different inputs. This page dissects the class anatomy, explains how one implementation plays two distinct probabilistic roles, traces the reparameterization trick, and documents the data-dependent KL divergence that binds the two encoders together during training.

## Role in the Conditional VAE

In classical VAEs, the prior is a fixed standard normal $\mathcal{N}(0, I)$, and only the posterior (recognition) network is learned. DeSCOPE departs from this convention: **both** distributions are amortized by neural networks and both are *conditional*. The prior encoder learns $p(z \mid x_{\text{ctrl}}, x_{\text{pert}})$ — a latent distribution predicted from the control cell profile and the perturbation embedding, i.e., what the model *believes* should happen under a perturbation. The posterior encoder learns $q_\phi(z \mid y, x_{\text{pert}})$ — a latent distribution inferred from the ground-truth perturbed expression profile, i.e., what actually *happened*. Training pulls these two distributions together via KL divergence, so that at inference time — when only the prior branch is available — sampling from the learned prior yields latents that the decoder can translate into realistic perturbed profiles.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Concept["Two Gaussian encoders, one class"]
        P["Prior encoder<br/>p(z | ctrl, pert)"]
        Q["Posterior encoder<br/>q(z | labels, pert)"]
    end
    Q -->|"KL divergence<br/>minimized"| P
    Q -->|"z provides<br/>decoder input"| D["Decoder"]
    P -->|"z provides<br/>decoder input<br/>at inference"| D
```

This prior/posterior split is why `forward` and `inference` in the model classes look asymmetric: training uses the posterior for reconstruction while measuring agreement with the prior; inference discards the posterior entirely and samples from the prior.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L36-L73), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L178-L196)

## One Class, Two Roles: The `VariationalEncoder`

Both encoders are instances of the same `VariationalEncoder(nn.Module)`, parameterized by an `in_dim` constructor argument. Internally it holds a single MLP built by `build_mlp`, configured to project `in_dim → hidden_size * 2`. The doubled output width is the design decision that fuses distribution parameterization into one linear layer: the final projection outputs a concatenated vector of width `2·hidden_size`, which `forward` splits into `mean` and `logvar` halves via `torch.chunk(chunks=2, dim=-1)`. There are no separate heads for the two moments — one matrix multiply produces both.

```python
self.encoder = build_mlp(
    in_dim=in_dim,
    out_dim=config.hidden_size * 2,  # mean, logvar
    hidden_dim=config.hidden_size,
    n_layers=self.n_encoder_layers,      # default: 4
    dropout=config.hidden_dropout,
    activation=ACT2FN[config.hidden_act],
    add_layernorm=config.add_layernorm
)
```

The forward pass returns a three-tuple — sampled latent, mean, and log-variance — leaving the consumption decision to the caller:

| Output | Shape | Training consumer | Inference consumer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z` | `(batch, hidden_size)` | Decoder (posterior only) | Decoder (prior only) |
| `mean` | `(batch, hidden_size)` | KL loss | Discarded |
| `logvar` | `(batch, hidden_size)` | KL loss | Discarded |

Two structural details of `build_mlp` matter for variational correctness. First, the **final projection layer carries no activation and no LayerNorm** — `mean` and `logvar` must be able to take any real value, so squashing them with GELU or normalizing them would corrupt the distribution parameterization. LayerNorm and activations are applied only to hidden layers. Second, the default depth of 4 layers (`variational_encoder_layers=4`) with `hidden_size=672` gives the block three GELU-transformed hidden layers followed by the bare moment projection.

| Layer index (4-layer config) | Structure |
|---|---|
| Hidden 1 | `Linear(in_dim → 672)` → `LayerNorm` → `GELU` → `Dropout` |
| Hidden 2–3 | `Linear(672 → 672)` → `LayerNorm` → `GELU` → `Dropout` |
| Output | `Linear(672 → 1344)` — no activation, no norm |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L36-L53), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L60-L73), [utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L103-L142), [configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28)

## Divergent Conditioning: What Each Encoder Sees

The two encoder instances are declared side by side in every model class with an identical input dimension — `in_dim = input_length + hidden_size` — but they are **separate modules with independent weights**; nothing is tied between them. Their probabilistic identities come entirely from what is concatenated into their inputs at call time:

- **Prior branch**: `torch.cat([ctrl_cell_expr, pert_embeddings], dim=-1)` — the control expression profile (TF-IDF normalized for ATAC, raw expression for RNA) concatenated with the perturbation embedding. No information about the true perturbed outcome enters this branch.
- **Posterior branch**: `torch.cat([labels, pert_embeddings], dim=-1)` — the ground-truth perturbed expression vector concatenated with the same perturbation embedding.

| Property | Prior encoder | Posterior encoder |
|---|---|---|
| Class | `VariationalEncoder` | `VariationalEncoder` |
| Input dim | `input_length + hidden_size` | `input_length + hidden_size` |
| Expression input | Control profile (`ctrl_cell_expr` / `ctrl_cell_tf_idf`) | Ground-truth perturbed profile (`labels`) |
| Conditioning shared input | `pert_embeddings` | `pert_embeddings` |
| Weights | Independent parameters | Independent parameters |
| Role in loss | KL target (learned prior) | KL source + reconstruction latent |
| Availability at inference | Active | Not invoked |

The asymmetric information access is the mechanism behind the model's inductive bias: because the posterior sees the answer and the prior does not, the KL term acts as a *conditional* regularizer that transfers perturbation-specific structure from the informative branch into the blind branch, rather than merely pulling latents toward a fixed standard normal.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L128-L130), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L214-L216), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L146-L151)

## Reparameterization and Latent Sampling

Gradient flow through a discrete sampling step would be broken, so `VariationalEncoder.reparameterize` implements the standard continuous relaxation. The log-variance is exponentiated to a standard deviation via `std = torch.exp(0.5 * logvar)`, Gaussian noise `eps = torch.randn_like(std)` is drawn, and the latent is reconstructed as `mean + eps * std`. This keeps the sampling operation differentiable with respect to both moments: gradients reach `mean` directly and reach `logvar` through the multiplicative noise path.

```python
def reparameterize(self, mean, logvar):
    std = torch.exp(0.5 * logvar)
    eps = torch.randn_like(std)
    return mean + eps * std
```

Note that the encoder's `forward` **always samples** — `z = self.reparameterize(mean, logvar)` runs unconditionally, even when the caller only needs the moments. During training, the prior's sampled `z` is immediately discarded (`_, prior_mean, prior_logvar = self.prior_encoder(...)`) because the KL divergence is computed analytically between closed-form Gaussians and requires no samples from the prior. The discarded sample costs a small amount of compute but has zero effect on gradients, since nothing downstream consumes it. Conversely, during inference the prior's moments are discarded and its `z` becomes the sole latent fed to the decoder.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L55-L58), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L67-L73), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L146-L148)

## Dataflow: Training versus Inference

The full picture of which branches are live in each mode:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Train["forward() — training"]
        C1["ctrl_cell_expr"] -->|"concat"| PI["prior_encoder"]
        PE1["pert_embeddings"] -->|"concat"| PI
        PE1 -->|"concat"| QI["posterior_encoder"]
        L1["labels (perturbed)"] -->|"concat"| QI
        PI -->|"μ_p, logvar_p only<br/>(z discarded)"| KL["kl_loss_func"]
        QI -->|"μ_q, logvar_q"| KL
        QI -->|"z_q"| DEC["decoder + softplus"]
        DEC --> MSE["MSE vs labels"]
        KL --> LOSS["α_mse·MSE + α_kl·KL"]
        MSE --> LOSS
    end
    subgraph Infer["inference() — no_grad"]
        C2["ctrl_cell_expr"] -->|"concat"| PI2["prior_encoder"]
        PE2["pert_embeddings"] -->|"concat"| PI2
        PI2 -->|"z_p only<br/>(moments discarded)"| DEC2["decoder + softplus"]
        DEC2 --> OUT["logits"]
    end
```

During training the posterior is the *workhorse*: its sampled latent `z_q` is concatenated with `pert_embeddings` and passed to the decoder, and its moments anchor one side of the KL computation. The prior contributes only its moments. During inference the roles invert: only the prior runs, its moments are thrown away, and its sampled `z` is the model's generative pathway from `(control, perturbation)` to predicted perturbed expression. The `inference` method is wrapped in `@torch.no_grad()` and never touches the posterior — it structurally guarantees that no ground-truth perturbed data leaks into prediction.

> [!TIP]
> The KL term is computed inside `torch.amp.autocast(enabled=False, device_type="cuda")` with explicit `.float()` casts on all four moment tensors. This is deliberate mixed-precision hygiene: `logvar.exp()` can overflow in fp16/bf16, and KL divergences are notoriously sensitive to precision loss. If you replicate this pattern elsewhere, disable autocast for the KL computation the same way.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L138-L176), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L178-L196), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L162-L168)

## The KL Term: Divergence Against a Learned Prior

Because the prior is a *learned* Gaussian rather than a fixed standard normal, DeSCOPE cannot use the textbook closed-form KL against $\mathcal{N}(0, I)$. Instead, `kl_loss_func` in `models/utils.py` implements the generalized KL divergence between two diagonal Gaussians:

$$D_{KL}(q \,\|\, p) = \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_j \left[ \log\frac{\sigma_{p,j}^2}{\sigma_{q,j}^2} + \frac{\sigma_{q,j}^2 + (\mu_{q,j} - \mu_{p,j})^2}{\sigma_{p,j}^2} - 1 \right]$$

implemented as:

```python
kl_loss = -0.5 * torch.sum(
    1
    + posterior_logvar
    - prior_logvar
    - (posterior_logvar.exp() + (posterior_mean - prior_mean).pow(2)) / prior_logvar.exp(),
    dim=-1
)
return kl_loss.mean()
```

The reduction strategy is worth reading precisely: the divergence is **summed across the latent dimension** (`dim=-1`, giving one scalar per cell) and then **averaged across the batch**, so the reported KL is the mean per-cell divergence. Every term is asymmetric in `prior`/`posterior` roles — swapping the argument order changes the value — so the call signature in `forward` (`prior moments first, posterior moments second`) is semantically load-bearing.

> [!TIP]
> If you modify the encoders' output layout — for example, changing the chunk order in `forward` or the moment split — remember that `kl_loss_func` receives positionally-matched tensors. The formula assumes the variance ratio uses the prior as denominator; a silent argument swap would still run without error but optimize the wrong divergence.

The scalar outputs of the prior/posterior pair — `mse_loss` and `kl_loss` — are combined as `loss = alpha_mse_loss * mse_loss + alpha_kl_loss * kl_loss` in the model's forward; the weighting defaults and tuning guidance live in the ELBO page, and the full loss composition is covered there.

Sources: [utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L28-L41), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L162-L169), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L248-L255)

## Configuration Surface

The encoders' shape and depth are governed by a small set of config fields, all exposed both on `DeSCOPEConfig` and as CLI arguments via `DeSCOPEModelArguments`. Training scripts thread them through directly when building the model from scratch.

| Parameter | Config field | CLI argument | Default | Effect on encoders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Latent/output width | `hidden_size` | `--hidden_size` | `672` | Hidden width; moments are `2 × 672` |
| Encoder depth | `variational_encoder_layers` | `--variational_encoder_layers` | `4` | MLP depth for **both** prior and posterior |
| Activation | `hidden_act` | `--hidden_act` | `"gelu"` | Hidden-layer activation |
| Hidden dropout | `hidden_dropout` | `--hidden_dropout` | `0` | Dropout on hidden layers |
| LayerNorm placement | `add_layernorm` | `--add_layernorm` | `True` | Norm on hidden layers (never on moment projection) |
| Expression input width | `input_length` | derived from dataset | `18080` | Prior/posterior `in_dim = input_length + hidden_size` |
| Perturbation embedding width | `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` | derived from ESM2 file | `5120` | Upstream of `pert_embeddings` (hidden_size after encoding) |

Note that `variational_encoder_layers` configures the prior and posterior *jointly* — there is no per-branch depth control. The one architectural asymmetry that does exist between model variants sits *upstream* of both encoders: `DeSCOPEForRNA` builds its `pert_gene_encoder` as a bare `Linear → LayerNorm` pair rather than the multi-layer `PertGeneEncoder` used by the ATAC variant, but since both reduce the perturbation embedding to `hidden_size`, the variational encoders' input dimension is identical across modalities.

Sources: [configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28), [arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L71-L85), [train.py](tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L54-L70), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L210-L216)

## Key Takeaways

Three facts anchor this subsystem for advanced readers. First, `VariationalEncoder` is a deliberately minimal design — one MLP, a doubled-width projection, a chunk, a reparameterization — and the entire prior/posterior distinction is expressed through call-site conditioning rather than class hierarchy. Second, the prior is conditional and learned, which makes the generalized KL formula with prior-variance denominators mandatory; standard-normal KL code is incompatible with this architecture. Third, the train/inference asymmetry (posterior-active vs prior-active) is enforced structurally in separate methods, so generative sampling at prediction time can never accidentally route through ground-truth labels.

Where to go next:

- How the perturbation embedding that conditions both encoders is produced: [PertGene Encoder and ESM2 Embeddings](8-pertgene-encoder-and-esm2-embeddings)
- What the decoder does with the sampled latent, including the softplus output head: [Decoder and Softplus Output Design](10-decoder-and-softplus-output-design)
- How the KL term combines with MSE into the full ELBO, including `alpha_kl_loss` tuning: [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition)
- The full set of tunable fields in context: [Model Configuration Reference](7-model-configuration-reference)
- Where the RNA/ATAC duplication (and the upstream `pert_gene_encoder` difference) fits in: [RNA and ATAC Model Variants](11-rna-and-atac-model-variants)


# Decoder and Softplus Output Design



This page dissects the **generation side** of DeSCOPE's conditional VAE: the `VariationalDecoder` that maps latent variables back into gene space, and the **softplus activation** applied to its raw outputs. The design makes two deliberate choices worth understanding: the decoder MLP terminates in a *bare linear head* with no internal output activation, and the softplus transform lives *outside* the decoder, at the model-wrapper level, so that both the training path (posterior sampling) and the inference path (prior sampling) share an identical output constraint. Both `DeSCOPEForRNA` and `DeSCOPEForATAC` reuse the exact same decoder construction, differing only in what feeds it.

## The VariationalDecoder: Structural Anatomy

The `VariationalDecoder` is a thin wrapper around the shared `build_mlp` factory. Its dimensions encode the cVAE contract: it accepts the concatenation of a latent vector `z` and the perturbation embedding (hence `in_dim = config.hidden_size * 2`), and emits a vector spanning the *entire* feature space (`out_dim = config.input_length`, defaulting to 18,080 genes/cCREs). Depth, width, and regularization are all delegated to config: `variational_decoder_layers` (default 4), `hidden_size` (default 672), `hidden_act` (default `gelu`), `hidden_dropout` (default 0), and `add_layernorm` (default `True`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph decoder_inputs["Decoder Inputs (concatenated)"]
        Z["z — latent sample<br/>(B × hidden_size)"]
        PE["pert_embeddings —<br/>(B × hidden_size)"]
    end
    subgraph VD["VariationalDecoder"]
        CAT["concat (dim=-1)<br/>(B × 2·hidden_size)"] --> MLP["MLP: 4 layers<br/>hidden = 672, GELU<br/>LayerNorm + Dropout"]
        MLP --> HEAD["Final Linear head<br/>672 → 18,080<br/>(no activation)"]
    end
    subgraph OUT["Model Wrapper"]
        SP["nn.functional.softplus"]
        SP --> LOGITS["Output.logits<br/>(B × input_length, ≥ 0)"]
    end
    Z --> CAT
    PE --> CAT
    HEAD --> SP
```

Note that the `forward` method is a pure pass-through — no activation, no normalization, no clipping. This is intentional: the decoder's contract is "produce raw real-valued logits," and constraint enforcement is deferred to the caller. The class is instantiated once per model (`self.decoder = VariationalDecoder(config, in_dim=config.hidden_size * 2)`) inside both `DeSCOPEForATAC` and `DeSCOPEForRNA`, meaning the two modalities share identical decoder code paths by construction.

| Decoder Parameter | Config Source | Default | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in_dim` | explicit arg | `hidden_size * 2` = 1,344 | Width of `[z ‖ pert_embedding]` concat |
| `out_dim` | `config.input_length` | 18,080 | Full gene/cCRE space reconstruction |
| Depth | `config.variational_decoder_layers` | 4 | Number of `Linear` blocks |
| Width | `config.hidden_size` | 672 | Hidden dimension throughout |
| Hidden activation | `ACT2FN[config.hidden_act]` | GELU | Nonlinearity *between* layers only |
| Regularization | `config.hidden_dropout` / `add_layernorm` | 0 / `True` | Applied to hidden states only |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L76-L98), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L1-L28), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L128-L130)

## Inside build_mlp: Layer Composition Rules

The decoder's internal structure is entirely determined by the `build_mlp` utility, which follows a strict composition grammar. For `n_layers ≥ 2`, each hidden block is `[Linear → (LayerNorm) → Activation → Dropout]`, and — critically — the **final layer is a bare `nn.Linear(hidden_dim, out_dim)`** with no norm, activation, or dropout attached. This guarantees the decoder emits unconstrained real values: normalization statistics are never computed *on* the output, and gradient flow into the final weights is unattenuated by any nonlinearity.

The `n_layers == 1` branch contains a subtle edge case worth knowing before you shrink the decoder: it appends `Linear(in_dim, out_dim)` and then, if `add_layernorm=True` (the default), a `LayerNorm(out_dim)` **on the decoder output itself**. This changes the semantics of the output layer compared to deeper configurations — the final affine transform would be re-centered per-sample to zero mean/unit variance before softplus, which compresses outputs into softplus's near-linear low regime and erases learned output scale.

> [!TIP]
> If you set `variational_decoder_layers=1` while leaving `add_layernorm=True`, the LayerNorm silently moves *inside* your output contract — applied directly on decoder logits. Keep `add_layernorm` semantics in mind whenever you deviate from the default 4-layer depth.

| Position in MLP | LayerNorm | Activation | Dropout | Applies to Decoder? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hidden layers 1…n−1 | ✅ if `add_layernorm` | ✅ GELU | ✅ `hidden_dropout` | Yes — all 3 hidden blocks (n=4) |
| Final layer (output) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Yes — bare linear, real-valued output |
| Single-layer mode (`n_layers=1`) | ⚠️ if `add_layernorm` | ❌ | ❌ | ⚠️ Norm lands on the **output** |

Sources: [utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L103-L142), [configuration_descope.py](/src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L18-L20)

## Softplus Output Activation: Placement and Properties

Immediately after every decoder call, the model wrappers apply `preds = nn.functional.softplus(preds)`. Softplus computes `log(1 + eˣ)`, a smooth, monotonic bijection from ℝ to (0, ∞). Its placement is architecturally meaningful: it lives in `DeSCOPEForATAC.forward`/`inference` and `DeSCOPEForRNA.forward`/`inference` — *not* inside the `VariationalDecoder` — so the transform is guaranteed to run on both the posterior-sampled training reconstruction and the prior-sampled inference prediction with the same semantics.

The choice of softplus over its competitors is driven by three properties that matter for expression-value regression:

1. **Non-negativity** — both scRNA-seq expression values and scATAC tf-idf scores are non-negative quantities; the output head must respect the data's support.
2. **Bounded gradients** — the derivative of softplus is `σ(x) ∈ (0, 1)`, so gradients flowing back through an 18,080-wide output layer are individually bounded, unlike `exp` whose gradient grows without bound and destabilizes wide regression heads.
3. **Smoothness everywhere** — unlike ReLU, there is no dead zone: every output neuron receives gradient, and the transition to the `x ≈ x` linear regime for large `x` preserves scale fidelity for highly expressed genes.

| Candidate Output Activation | Range | Gradient Behavior | Fit for Expression Regression |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Softplus** (chosen) | (0, ∞) | `σ(x)`, bounded in (0,1) | Smooth, unbounded above, stable ✅ |
| ReLU | [0, ∞) | 0 or 1, kink at 0 | Dead neurons; non-differentiable ❌ |
| `exp` | (0, ∞) | `eˣ`, unbounded | Exploding outputs/gradients ❌ |
| Sigmoid × scale | (0, scale) | Bounded but saturating | Artificial ceiling on expression ❌ |
| Identity | ℝ | 1 | Violates non-negativity of data ❌ |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L152-L153), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L188-L189), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L238-L239), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L274-L275)

## Dual-Path Decoding: One Head, Two Latent Sources

The same decoder instance and the same softplus transform serve two distinct dataflows, differing only in the provenance of `z`. During **training**, the posterior encoder produces `posterior_z` (the reparameterized sample given the ground-truth labels), which is concatenated with the perturbation embedding and decoded; the softplus-transformed output then enters the MSE loss against `labels`. During **inference**, the posterior is unavailable — there are no perturbed labels — so the prior encoder (conditioned on control cells) supplies `prior_z` instead. The decoder weights and output transform are therefore shared, and the train/inference gap is isolated to exactly one input tensor.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph TRAIN["Training Path (forward)"]
        L["labels (ground truth)"] --> POST["posterior_encoder"] --> PZ["posterior_z"]
        PZ --> DEC1["VariationalDecoder"]
        EMB1["pert_embeddings"] --> DEC1
        DEC1 --> SP1["softplus"] --> MSE["MSE loss vs labels"]
    end
    subgraph INF["Inference Path (inference)"]
        CTRL["ctrl cell expr / tf-idf"] --> PRIOR["prior_encoder"] --> PRZ["prior_z"]
        PRZ --> DEC2["VariationalDecoder (same weights)"]
        EMB2["pert_embeddings"] --> DEC2
        DEC2 --> SP2["softplus"] --> OUT["Output.logits<br/>(no_grad)"]
    end
```

This symmetry has a practical consequence: because softplus is applied identically in both paths, evaluation metrics computed on inference outputs are directly comparable to training-time MSE — there is no train/serve skew in the output transform. The inference method is additionally decorated with `@torch.no_grad()`, so the entire decoder–softplus chain runs in inference mode with no autograd overhead.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L146-L153), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L178-L189), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L232-L239), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L264-L275)

## Downstream Consumption: Loss, Precision, and the Output Container

The softplus-transformed predictions are consumed in two places. First, the **loss**: element-wise MSE is computed between `softplus(preds)` and `labels` via `nn.functional.mse_loss(..., reduction="none")`, then optionally reweighted by a per-feature `mse_weights` tensor before reduction. Second, the **output container**: predictions are returned in the `logits` field of `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` / `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` (`ModelOutput` dataclasses) alongside the decomposed `loss`, `mse_loss`, and `kl_loss`. The `logits` name is conventional rather than literal — these are post-softplus, non-negative expression predictions, not unnormalized scores, and downstream evaluation code should treat them as final values.

One precision detail adjacent to the decoder output: the KL term is computed under `torch.amp.autocast(enabled=False)` with explicit `.float()` casts, while the MSE over softplus outputs runs under standard autocast precision. This split reflects the relative numerical sensitivities of the two loss branches — KL divergences involve exponentials of log-variances that degrade badly in fp16, whereas MSE on bounded-gradient softplus outputs is tolerant of reduced precision.

> [!TIP]
> The two model variants reweight weighted-MSE differently: `DeSCOPEForATAC` reduces with `(weights * elementwise).sum(dim=-1).mean()`, while `DeSCOPEForRNA` uses `(weights * elementwise).mean()`. If you port `mse_weights` between modalities, the ATAC weighting scales per-cell losses by the weight magnitude while RNA normalizes it away — verify your expected loss scale after any transfer.

| Output Field | Contents | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `logits` | `softplus(decoder([z ‖ pert_emb]))` — non-negative, shape `(B, input_length)` | Evaluation metrics, downstream analyses |
| `mse_loss` | Weighted/unweighted MSE on softplus outputs | Training logging, early stopping |
| `kl_loss` | Prior–posterior KL in fp32 (autocast disabled) | Training logging, ELBO composition |
| `loss` | `alpha_mse_loss · mse_loss + alpha_kl_loss · kl_loss` | Backpropagation |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L155-L169), [modeling_descope.py](/src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L241-L255), [utils.py](/src/descope/models/utils.py#L12-L25)

## Design Rationale: Deterministic Regression over Probabilistic Heads

The codebase carries a `ZINBLoss` module (a zero-inflated negative-binomial likelihood with clamping for numerical stability and a sampling method) — but neither `DeSCOPEForRNA` nor `DeSCOPEForATAC` uses it. The main models commit to **deterministic MSE regression on softplus-bounded outputs**, a choice consistent with a tf-idf/expression-space reconstruction target rather than raw count modeling. The ZINB machinery remains available in `utils.py` as a fallback for workflows that genuinely require count-distribution likelihoods (e.g., raw UMI data without normalization), but the shipped training scripts optimize the MSE+KL objective exclusively.

| Design Dimension | MSE + Softplus (shipped) | ZINB Head (available, unused) |
|---|---|---|
| Output | Point prediction per feature | Distribution parameters (μ, θ, π) |
| Decoder head | Single `Linear → input_length` | Three heads or feature stacking |
| Loss stability | Trivially stable, bounded gradients | Requires clamping (`eps=1e-4`), `lgamma` precision care |
| Target data | Normalized expression / tf-idf | Raw integer counts with dropouts |
| Autocast compatibility | Tolerant of mixed precision | Currently force-cast to fp32 |

This completes the generation pathway: encoder outputs → variational sampling → **decoder MLP (bare linear head) → softplus → non-negative reconstruction**, with the KL branch safeguarded in fp32. For how the two variational sources of `z` are produced, continue to [Prior and Posterior Variational Encoders](9-prior-and-posterior-variational-encoders); for how the softplus output feeds the ELBO objective, see [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition); for modality-specific differences upstream of the decoder, see [RNA and ATAC Model Variants](11-rna-and-atac-model-variants).


# RNA and ATAC Model Variants



DeSCOPE ships **one conditional VAE (CVAE) design expressed as two concrete HuggingFace model classes**: `DeSCOPEForATAC` and `DeSCOPEForRNA`. At first glance they look like near-duplicates — and that is intentional. The codebase documents this choice explicitly: *"The RNA and ATAC models have identical architectures; we maintain them as two distinct models to support independent adjustment for each data modality."* This page explains why the split exists, where the variants genuinely diverge (a modality-specific input contract, a different perturbation-encoder implementation, and a subtle loss-aggregation asymmetry), and how each variant pairs with its tokenizer, dataset, and inference classes. For the mathematical core shared by both variants, start with [Conditional VAE Architecture Overview](6-conditional-vae-architecture-overview).

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L118), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L199-L200)

## One Config, Two Model Classes

Both variants consume the same `DeSCOPEConfig` (`model_type = "descope"`), whose defaults reveal the shared design: `input_length=18080` carries the inline comment `# rna, atac`, meaning both modalities target the same feature-space width (18,080 genes for RNA, 18,080 top-ranked cCREs for ATAC), and `input_pert_gene_embedding_size=5120` matches ESM2 protein embeddings for the perturbed gene. Neither class overrides the config; every dimension flows from this single source of truth, which is why hyperparameters in the RNA and ATAC tutorial shell scripts are byte-for-byte identical.

Sources: [configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28), [train_descope.sh](tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train_descope.sh#L10-L17), [train_descope.sh](tutorials/RNA_Gene/train_descope.sh#L10-L17)

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DeSCOPEConfig {
        +model_type = "descope"
        +hidden_size = 672
        +input_length = 18080
        +input_pert_gene_embedding_size = 5120
    }
    class DeSCOPEPretrainedModel {
        <<HuggingFace base>>
        +config_class = DeSCOPEConfig
    }
    class DeSCOPEForATAC {
        +pert_gene_encoder : PertGeneEncoder
        +forward(ctrl_cell_tf_idf, ...)
        +inference(ctrl_cell_tf_idf, ...)
    }
    class DeSCOPEForRNA {
        +pert_gene_encoder : Linear+LayerNorm
        +forward(ctrl_cell_expr, ...)
        +inference(ctrl_cell_expr, ...)
    }
    class DeSCOPEForATACOutput {
        loss / mse_loss / kl_loss / logits
    }
    class DeSCOPEForRNAOutput {
        loss / mse_loss / kl_loss / logits
    }
    DeSCOPEPretrainedModel <|-- DeSCOPEForATAC
    DeSCOPEPretrainedModel <|-- DeSCOPEForRNA
    DeSCOPEForATAC ..> DeSCOPEForATACOutput
    DeSCOPEForRNA ..> DeSCOPEForRNAOutput
    DeSCOPEConfig ..> DeSCOPEPretrainedModel
```

The shared component classes — `PertGeneEncoder` (ESM2 5120-d → hidden 672 via `build_mlp`), `VariationalEncoder` (concatenated control vector + perturbation embedding → factorized Gaussian mean/logvar with the reparameterization trick), and `VariationalDecoder` (z + perturbation embedding → `input_length` logits passed through `softplus`) — are instantiated identically inside both variants' `__init__`. The output dataclasses `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` and `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` are also field-identical (loss, mse_loss, kl_loss, logits); the type split exists purely so downstream trainer and evaluation code stays modality-explicit.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L15-L33), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L36-L98), [utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L12-L25), [utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L103-L142)

## Where the Variants Actually Differ

Diffing the two classes line by line yields exactly three functional deltas: the perturbation encoder construction, the control-cell input tensor (name and semantics), and the weighted-MSE reduction. Everything else — forward-pass data flow, softplus output activation, KL computation under disabled autocast, and the prior-sampling `inference` path — is verbatim-parallel code.

| Dimension | `DeSCOPEForATAC` | `DeSCOPEForRNA` |
|---|---|---|
| Control input kwarg | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` | `ctrl_cell_expr` |
| Input semantics | TF-IDF-normalized cCRE accessibility vector | library-normalized expression (`target_sum=1e4`) |
| `pert_gene_encoder` | `PertGeneEncoder` (`build_mlp`, honors `pert_gene_encoder_layers` / `add_layernorm` CLI args) | Hard-coded `nn.Sequential(Linear(5120→672), LayerNorm(672))` |
| Output dataclass | `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` | `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` |
