It builds a cache mapping each perturbation to its top-k genes by sorting the real DE CSV on `fdr` ascending, then uses `bulk_array.perturbation_effect(which="pred"/"real")` to obtain Δ vectors. `direction_match_on_topk_de` follows the same caching pattern but computes sign-agreement accuracy (`np.mean(np.sign(x_de) == np.sign(y_de))`), and can stratify results into up-regulated (`percent_change > 0`) and down-regulated (`percent_change < 0`) gene sets — yielding four return values when `separate_up_down_regulated=True`.

`edistance` is architecturally different: it takes a single AnnData (not a pair) and computes the energy distance `2·E[‖X−Y‖] − E[‖X−X′‖] − E[‖Y−Y′‖]` between each perturbation group and the control group, using `sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances`. Its performance optimization is worth noting — the within-control distance `sigma_y` is precomputed once and reused across all perturbations rather than recomputed per iteration.

> [!TIP]
> The top-k DE metrics read `real_de.csv` — the DE table cell-eval writes to `outdir` for the *real* AnnData — not the predicted DE. This is intentional: the metric asks "how well do predicted effects agree with ground-truth effects on genes the ground truth says matter?" If you delete the outdir before computing extra metrics, re-run `compute_metrics` first or generate the DE table independently with `build_de`.

Sources: [utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L844-L890), [utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L640-L707), [utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L710-L841), [utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L893-L971)

## Supporting Infrastructure: DE Computation and Skipping Logic

Two supporting mechanisms make the system efficient at scale. The first is `build_de` in `utils.py`, a standalone differential-expression utility that wraps `pdex.parallel_differential_expression` (the `pdex` package, also pinned in `pyproject.toml`). It asserts log-normalization via `wppkg.guess_is_lognorm` (unless `check_log_norm=False`), builds pdex kwargs referencing the control group and perturbation column, and writes `de.csv` to an optional outdir — the same format cell-eval produces, making it a compatible substitute when you need DE tables without a full evaluation run.

The second is the DE-skipping decision embedded in `compute_metrics`. The private helper `check_whether_skip_de_metrics` intersects the requested metric names with `all_de_metrics`; if no DE-type metric is requested, `skip_de=True` is passed to `MetricsEvaluator`, avoiding the most expensive stage of evaluation (per-perturbation Wilcoxon tests via pdex). For large perturbation panels this can cut evaluation time substantially — but remember that skipping DE also means no `real_de.csv` is written, so the top-k extra metrics cannot run afterward.

Sources: [utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L974-L1019), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L118-L158), [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L15-L22)

## End-to-End Evaluation Workflow

The complete evaluation flow, as exercised in the Sciplex3 zero-shot notebook, chains prediction generation, format assembly, metric computation, and artifact persistence. Note the strict guard in the inference stage: `use_generated_control_cells` is asserted `False` at the source level because substituting model-generated control cells makes results unstable — the final predicted AnnData always concatenates *real* control cells from `_organize_final_results`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[InferenceForRNA init<br/>test CSV template + ground-truth h5ad] --> B[inference<br/>generate perturbed cells per template]
    B --> C["_organize_final_results<br/>replace generated ctrl with real ctrl"]
    C --> D["compute_metrics<br/>monkey-patch validation bypass"]
    D --> E["MetricsEvaluator<br/>skip_de decision + PDex DE"]
    E --> F["results + agg_results<br/>Polars DataFrames"]
    E --> G["evaluator.anndata_pair<br/>+ real_de.csv in outdir"]
    G --> H["extra_metrics_func<br/>pearson / topk-DE metrics / edistance"]
    F --> I["Aggregate per-perturbation CSV"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["write_h5ad<br/>persist predictions"]
```

In the notebook, this translates to: select metrics from `infer.all_metrics`; optionally subset both AnnData objects to reliably predicted genes; call `compute_metrics(...)` receiving `(results, agg_results, evaluator)`; then compute extra metrics against `evaluator.anndata_pair` and `./cell-eval-outdir/{celltype}/real_de.csv`. The final aggregation maps the per-perturbation dicts onto the built-in `results` frame by `perturbation` key and writes `results_for_each_perturbation.csv`, giving a single unified per-drug scorecard.

Sources: [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L286-L348), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L350-L370), [2_inference.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/zero-shot/2_inference.ipynb#L44-L245)

## Artifact Contract of the Output Directory

Every `compute_metrics` call materializes artifacts into `outdir` (default `./cell-eval-outdir`), which becomes both a debugging aid and a dependency for downstream extra metrics:

| Artifact | Producer | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `real_de.csv` / `pred_de.csv` | cell-eval (pdex DE) | `pearson_delta_on_topk_de`, `direction_match_on_topk_de` |
| `results`, `agg_results` frames | `evaluator.compute()` | final aggregation step |
| `descope_preds.h5ad` | `infer.write_h5ad(...)` | reproducibility / later re-analysis |

The tutorial parameterizes the outdir per cell type (`./cell-eval-outdir/{celltype}`) since Sciplex3 evaluation loops over multiple cell lines (e.g., A549), keeping each panel's DE tables and per-perturbation CSVs isolated.

Sources: [2_inference.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/zero-shot/2_inference.ipynb#L126-L137), [2_inference.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/zero-shot/2_inference.ipynb#L164-L245), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L243-L247)

## Where to Go Next

The evaluation layer sits at the end of the model lifecycle, so its inputs are defined upstream. To understand how `adata_pred` is generated — the control-cell sampling loop, gene-embedding injection, and NaN-batch rejection — see [Inference Pipeline Design](19-inference-pipeline-design). The leave-one-out protocol that structures which perturbations land in the test template is covered in [Leave-One-Out Evaluation Protocol](21-leave-one-out-evaluation-protocol), while zero-shot versus fine-tuned evaluation on Sciplex3 and Tahoe-100M — the setting where these metrics were used to produce the published performance figures — is detailed in [Zero-Shot and Fine-Tuning Workflows](22-zero-shot-and-fine-tuning-workflows). For a hands-on walkthrough including training, follow [Tutorial Pipeline: Tokenize, Train, Evaluate](4-tutorial-pipeline-tokenize-train-evaluate).


# Leave-One-Out Evaluation Protocol



This page documents how DeSCOPE quantifies **cross-context generalization** through its leave-one-out (LOO) evaluation protocol: for each evaluation target, the protocol withholds the target from pretraining, trains in two stages (pretrain → fine-tune), and scores predictions strictly on a pre-registered set of held-out test perturbations. We trace the full path from data splits (`Test_Info` CSVs, `loo_*` tokenized corpora) through the two-stage training scripts to the cell-eval-based scoring stack in `inference.py`.

## Protocol at a Glance

In the RNA_Gene tutorial, the protocol iterates over five cell lines — `H1`, `K562_ESSENTIAL`, `JURKAT`, `RPE1`, `HEPG2`. For each target cell line `cellline_ft`, the "left-out" set is the target itself: the pretraining corpus is built from the remaining four lines (`cellline_pt = [c for c in cellline if c != cellline_ft]`), while the target's own test perturbations — enumerated in `Test_Info_{cellline_ft}.csv` — are excluded from its training tokenization. The result per fold is three disjoint artifacts: (1) a cross-cell-line pretraining corpus `tokenized_dataset/loo_{cellline_ft}` that never contains the target line, (2) a target-line training split with test perturbations filtered out, and (3) the target-line test perturbations used only at scoring time. The `DeSCOPE_LOO` model produced by this loop is then compared against standard `DeSCOPE` training to isolate the contribution of pretraining on other cell lines.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Splits["Per-fold data artifacts (fold = HEPG2 as example)"]
        TI["Test_Info_HEPG2.csv<br/>(held-out test perturbations)"]
        FT["HEPG2/tokenized_dataset<br/>(target train split, test perts excluded)"]
        LOO["tokenized_dataset/loo_HEPG2<br/>(pretrain corpus: H1, K562_ESSENTIAL,<br/>JURKAT, RPE1 — target line absent)"]
    end
    subgraph Stages["Two-stage training"]
        P["Stage 1: Pretrain<br/>on loo_HEPG2"]
        F["Stage 2: Fine-tune<br/>init from pretrain/last_model<br/>data = HEPG2 train split"]
    end
    E["InferenceForRNA<br/>score on Test_Info_HEPG2 perturbations"]
    LOO --> P --> F
    FT --> F
    TI -.->|defines evaluation set| E
    F --> E
```

The diagram's prerequisite: read `loo_{X}` as "pretraining corpus for the fold whose fine-tune target is X" — the naming encodes which cell line was left out of pretraining, not which data the corpus contains.

Sources: [tokenize.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/tokenize.ipynb#L19-L77), [train_descope_loo.sh](tutorials/RNA_Gene/train_descope_loo.sh#L4-L8), [README.md](tutorials/RNA_Gene/README.md#L11-L24)

## The Held-Out Boundary: Test Perturbations and Control Preservation

The boundary between "trainable" and "evaluable" data is enforced at tokenization time by `_filter_perturbations`. Its contract is strict and matters for protocol integrity: `perts_to_include` and `perts_to_exclude` are mutually exclusive (specifying both raises `ValueError`), perturbation labels are whitespace-stripped before matching, and — critically — **control cells are always preserved**: in exclude mode, `ctrl_name` is removed from the exclusion list before filtering; in include mode, it is appended if absent. In the tutorial's Section 1, every cell line is tokenized with `perts_to_exclude=load_gene_names_engine(Test_Info_{c}.csv)`, so the shipped training datasets structurally cannot contain the perturbations later used for scoring, while control cells survive as the conditioning baseline for prediction.

| Filter configuration | Cells retained | Control handling |
|---|---|---|
| `perts_to_include` only | Cells whose label ∈ include list | `ctrl_name` force-appended to the list |
| `perts_to_exclude` only | Cells whose label ∉ exclude list | `ctrl_name` force-removed from the list |
| Both `None` | All cells | Unconditional retention |
| Both specified | — | Rejected with `ValueError` |

> [!TIP]
> Control-cell preservation inside `_filter_perturbations` is what makes the evaluation sound: inference conditions every prediction on real control cells, so an exclusion filter that dropped controls would silently corrupt the entire protocol.

Sources: [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L23-L47), [tokenize.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/tokenize.ipynb#L31-L47)

One subtlety worth internalizing: leakage prevention is **scoped per fold, not global**. Section 2 of `tokenize.ipynb` reads the pretraining lines' raw `.h5ad` files directly and passes `apply_pert_gene_filter=False`, meaning each `loo_*` corpus retains *all* perturbations present in the non-target lines — including those lines' own `Test_Info` perturbations. Only the fold's target line has its test perturbations withheld. This is deliberate: the hypothesis under test is transfer from other cell contexts to the target, not perturbation-level memorization within the target.

Sources: [tokenize.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/tokenize.ipynb#L49-L77), [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L586-L598)

## Assembling the Cross-Cell-Line Pretraining Corpora

`TokenizerForRNA` solves the hard constraint of multi-dataset pretraining: heterogeneous cell lines must be projected into a single model input space. On construction with the fold's fine-tune line, `__init__` extracts two registries from the target AnnData — `input_genes_list` (gene symbols from `var_names`, after dropping cells with null perturbation labels) and `pert_genes_list` (the target's unique perturbation labels). Every pretraining line is then tokenized by `_tokenize`, which aligns its feature axis onto `input_genes_list` via `UniformFeatureForAnnData` (with `DuplicatedFeatureHandling.max_pooling` to collapse duplicate gene symbols across platforms), restores the pretraining line's original perturbation labels, and applies `preprocess_rna_perturbation_adata` (library-size normalization to `target_sum` + `log1p`, with an optional raw-counts integer check). The tutorial disables `apply_pert_gene_filter`, so no cells are dropped for having perturbations unseen in the target line.

Each pretraining line is persisted as an independent Hugging Face Dataset under `save_dir/{cell_line_name}` inside the `loo_{cellline_ft}` directory — so `tokenize()` produces, per fold, a directory of per-line Arrow datasets (e.g., `loo_HEPG2/H1`, `loo_HEPG2/JURKAT`, …). Per-dataset configuration variability is handled in the loop itself: `H1` uses `pert_col="target_gene"` and `target_sum=5e4`, the other lines use `pert_col="gene"` and `target_sum=1e4`. The notebook also flags a protocol-level invariant: **control-cell names must be identical across all `.h5ad` files**, since `ctrl_name` is a single global parameter consumed identically by training and inference.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["For each fold X in {H1, K562, JURKAT, RPE1, HEPG2}"] --> B["TokenizerForRNA(cell_line_ft=X.h5ad)<br/>→ input_genes_list, pert_genes_list"]
    B --> C["tokenize(cell_line_pt = all lines except X)"]
    C --> D["Per line: align features to X's genes<br/>(UniformFeatureForAnnData, max_pooling)"]
    D --> E["Normalize: target_sum → log1p<br/>(optional raw-count check)"]
    E --> F["Save HF Dataset<br/>tokenized_dataset/loo_X/{line}"]
    F --> G{"Next fold?"}
    G -->|yes| A
    G -->|no| H["5 × loo_* corpora ready<br/>+ 5 × per-line fine-tune splits (Section 1)"]
```

| `TokenizerForRNA` parameter | Role in the LOO corpora | Tutorial value |
|---|---|---|
| `cell_line_ft` | Defines the unified gene space & perturbation registry | The left-out target line's `.h5ad` |
| `input_genes_list` | Feature-alignment target for every pretraining line | From `cell_line_ft.var_names` |
| `apply_pert_gene_filter` | Whether pretraining cells are restricted to target-line perturbations | `False` (keep all) |
| `duplicated_features_handling` | Merges duplicate gene symbols during alignment | `max_pooling` |
| `target_sum` | Library-size normalization depth | `1e4` (or `5e4` for H1) |
| `save_dir` | Per-fold corpus root; subdirectory per pretraining line | `tokenized_dataset/loo_{ft}` |

Sources: [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L517-L552), [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L554-L631), [tokenize.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/tokenize.ipynb#L49-L77)

## Stage Structure: Pretrain, Then Fine-Tune

`train_descope_loo.sh` operationalizes the fold as two sequential `accelerate launch train.py` invocations that share `MODELPARAMS`, `DATAPARAMS`, and `TRAINPARAMS` (seed 42, 20 epochs, cosine LR `1e-4`, bf16, per-device batch 64, `alpha_mse_loss=alpha_kl_loss=1.0`). Stage 1 points `--tokenized_datasets_dir` at the `loo_K562_ESSENTIAL` corpus and writes to a dedicated `trainer_output_pretrain` directory. Stage 2 re-launches training with two changes: `--pretrained_model_name_or_path="$pretrain_output_dir/last_model"` initializes weights from the pretraining run's final checkpoint, and `--tokenized_datasets_dir` switches to the target line's Section-1 dataset (test perturbations already excluded). Output directories are deliberately separated (`trainer_output_pretrain` vs `trainer_output_finetune` under `./results/descope_loo/`) so the stage handoff is explicit on disk.

| Dimension | Standard (`train_descope.sh`) | LOO (`train_descope_loo.sh`) |
|---|---|---|
| Training stages | Single run on the target line's split | Pretrain on N−1 other lines → fine-tune on target split |
| Initialization | Random | `pretrain_output_dir/last_model` |
| Data seen by the target line | Train split only (test perts excluded) | Identical — plus prior exposure to *other* lines |
| Output layout | `results/descope/trainer_output/` | `results/descope_loo/trainer_output_{pretrain,finetune}/` |
| What the eval measures | In-line prediction of unseen perturbations | Marginal gain from cross-cell-line pretraining |
| Cost | 1 training run per line | 2 runs × 5 folds (per-fold pretraining is fold-specific) |

The trade-off is symmetric: the standard configuration is cheaper and answers "can the model generalize to new perturbations within a line?", whereas LOO answers the strictly stronger question "does pretraining on other cell lines improve that generalization?" — at the price of re-running the pretraining stage for every fold, since each fold's corpus must exclude a different line. For the ATAC modality, the `ATAC_Gene` tutorial ships the same script pair, applying an analogous protocol over ATAC perturbation data (see [RNA and ATAC Model Variants](11-rna-and-atac-model-variants)).

Sources: [train_descope_loo.sh](tutorials/RNA_Gene/train_descope_loo.sh#L4-L84), [train_descope.sh](tutorials/RNA_Gene/train_descope.sh#L1-L59)

## Scoring the Held-Out Perturbations

Evaluation runs in `test.ipynb` against the fine-tuned checkpoint. `InferenceForRNA` is constructed with four protocol-critical arguments: `test_csv_template_fp=Test_Info_{line}.csv` (re-registering the held-out perturbation set for prediction), the target line's raw `.h5ad` (source of real control cells and ground truth), the fine-tune checkpoint path, and the same `pert_col`/`ctrl_name`/`target_sum` contract used at tokenization. The `infer.inference()` call then predicts responses for every held-out perturbation, conditioned on `gene_embs_file` (the ESM2-derived perturbation-gene embedding table shared with training — see [PertGene Encoder and ESM2 Embeddings](8-pertgene-encoder-and-esm2-embeddings)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant NB as test.ipynb
    participant IF as InferenceForRNA
    participant TI as Test_Info CSV + target .h5ad
    participant CE as cell_eval.MetricsEvaluator
    participant XM as extra_metrics_func
    NB->>IF: __init__(test_csv_template_fp, adata, checkpoint)
    NB->>IF: inference(gene_embs_file, use_generated_control_cells=False)
    IF->>TI: load held-out perts, real control cells, ground truth
    IF-->>NB: adata_pred, adata_test_ground_truth
    NB->>IF: compute_metrics(adata_pred, adata_real, metrics_to_calculate)
    IF->>CE: MetricsEvaluator(..., de_method="wilcoxon")
    CE-->>NB: results, agg_results, evaluator
    NB->>XM: pearson / pearson_delta_on_topk_de / direction_match_on_topk_de
    XM-->>NB: per-perturbation values (merged into results CSV)
```

Two implementation details in `inference.py` are essential to reading the numbers correctly. First, `compute_metrics` deliberately monkey-patches `cell_eval._evaluator._build_anndata_pair` with `_build_anndata_pair_NOCHECK`, bypassing cell-eval's log1p-format validation — the docstring states this exists because model outputs may be raw or non-log-transformed (e.g., negative values); if you want validated comparison, the private `_compute_metrics` remains available. Second, the notebook's evaluation contract mandates `use_generated_control_cells=False` — predictions must be conditioned on *real* control cells from the target `.h5ad`, never synthesized ones.

> [!TIP]
> Never flip `use_generated_control_cells=True` in the LOO evaluation: the protocol's claim is about generalization to held-out perturbations measured against real experimental controls, and generated controls would change the quantity being measured.

Sources: [test.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/test.ipynb#L10-L48), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L19-L45), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L113-L146)

The metric layer combines cell-eval's registry with DeSCOPE-specific extras. `CellEvalMixin.all_metrics` exposes the library's full metric registry; the notebook selects a subset for the aggregate report, while `extra_metrics_func` provides custom implementations attached to the returned `evaluator.anndata_pair`. Metrics are computed per perturbation and aggregated; `results.to_pandas()` is enriched with the extra-metric columns and exported as `results_for_each_perturbation.csv`, alongside the predicted AnnData via `infer.write_h5ad` (the `real_de.csv` produced by the wilcoxon DE pass feeds the top-k DE metrics).

| Metric | Source | What it captures |
|---|---|---|
| `pearson_delta` | cell-eval built-in | Correlation of predicted vs real *perturbation deltas* (vs control) |
| `overlap_at_50/100/200/500` | cell-eval built-in | Top-N DE gene overlap between prediction and ground truth |
| `discrimination_score_l1` | cell-eval built-in | L1-based separation of perturbed from control profiles |
| `mae` | cell-eval built-in | Absolute expression error |
| `pearson` | `extra_metrics_func` | Profile-level correlation, averaged across perturbations |
| `pearson_delta_on_topk_de` (topk=20) | `extra_metrics_func` | Delta accuracy restricted to top-20 ground-truth DE genes |
| `direction_match_on_topk_de` (topk=100, up/down split) | `extra_metrics_func` | Sign agreement on top-100 up- and down-regulated DE genes |
| `edistance` | `extra_metrics_func` | available E-distance metric on the AnnData pair |

Sources: [test.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/test.ipynb#L50-L127), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L47-L111), [test.ipynb](tutorials/RNA_Gene/test.ipynb#L129-L151)

## Interpreting Results and Where to Go Next

Interpretation follows the fold structure: each fold yields one `results_for_each_perturbation.csv` whose rows are the perturbations registered in `Test_Info_{line}.csv`, so per-perturbation failures (e.g., low `direction_match` on specific genes) can be traced individually, while `agg_results` supports the headline DeSCOPE-vs-DeSCOPE_LOO comparison. Because the only experimental variable between the two arms is the pretraining corpus (identical fine-tune data, seed, hyperparameters, and evaluation set), any aggregate delta is attributable to cross-cell-line pretraining — which is precisely the claim the protocol is designed to isolate. When extending the protocol to new modalities or datasets, preserve its three invariants: test perturbations excluded from the target's training split, target line absent from its own fold's pretraining corpus, and evaluation conditioned on real control cells. For deeper mechanics, continue with [Perturbation Metrics via Cell-Eval](20-perturbation-metrics-via-cell-eval) for the metric implementations, [Inference Pipeline Design](19-inference-pipeline-design) for the prediction internals, [Zero-Shot and Fine-Tuning Workflows](22-zero-shot-and-fine-tuning-workflows) for how this protocol generalizes to other transfer scenarios, and [Tokenization: AnnData to HuggingFace Datasets](12-tokenization-anndata-to-huggingface-datasets) / [Feature Alignment and Vocabulary Handling](14-feature-alignment-and-vocabulary-handling) for the corpus-construction layer. The end-to-end reproduction guide remains [Tutorial Pipeline: Tokenize, Train, Evaluate](4-tutorial-pipeline-tokenize-train-evaluate).


# Zero-Shot and Fine-Tuning Workflows



DeSCOPE exposes two distinct paths for applying a model to perturbation prediction: the **zero-shot workflow**, where a pretrained checkpoint is used directly for inference on new perturbations without any gradient updates, and the **fine-tuning workflow**, where the same checkpoint serves as weight initialization for continued training on target data. Both paths share one infrastructure component — the `pretrained_model_name_or_path` switch — but diverge in entry point, data requirements, and evaluation semantics. This page documents both workflows as implemented in `src/descope/` and demonstrated across the three tutorial suites, at the boundary between the training system and the inference/evaluation system.

## The Central Switch: `pretrained_model_name_or_path`

The entire zero-shot vs. fine-tuning distinction in DeSCOPE reduces to a single optional field on `DeSCOPETrainingArguments`:

```python
pretrained_model_name_or_path: Optional[str] = field(
    default=None, metadata={"help": "Path to a pretrained model."}
)
```

Every training entry script in the repository follows an identical branching pattern around this value. When it is `None`, a fresh `DeSCOPEConfig` is built from the dataset shapes and `DeSCOPEModelArguments`, and training proceeds from random initialization. When it points to a checkpoint directory, the model is reconstructed via the Hugging Face `from_pretrained` interface with only the loss weights (`alpha_mse_loss`, `alpha_kl_loss`) supplied as overrides:

```python
if train_args.pretrained_model_name_or_path is None:
    config = DeSCOPEConfig(...)          # from model_args + dataset shapes
    model = DeSCOPEForRNA(config=config, ...)
else:
    model = DeSCOPEForRNA.from_pretrained(
        train_args.pretrained_model_name_or_path,
        alpha_mse_loss=train_args.alpha_mse_loss,
        alpha_kl_loss=train_args.alpha_kl_loss
    )
```

This gives fine-tuning zero additional code: the model branch changes, while the dataset, trainer, and evaluation loop remain byte-for-byte identical to standard training.

Sources: [arguments.py](/src/descope/arguments.py#L18-L22), [2_train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/fine-tune/2_train.py#L56-L81), [train.py](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train.py#L52-L77)

## The Zero-Shot Workflow: Inference Without Adaptation

Zero-shot evaluation answers one question: *how well does a checkpoint predict perturbations it has never trained on?* The implementation lives entirely in `src/descope/inference.py`, which provides modality-specific subclasses (`InferenceForRNA`, `InferenceForATAC`) of an abstract `BaseInference`. No training code is invoked at any point.

The workflow proceeds in three stages, orchestrated in the tutorial notebooks:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Pretrained checkpoint<br/>e.g. descope-tahoe100m-12059-hvgs] --> B[InferenceForRNA /<br/>InferenceForATAC init]
    C[Ground-truth AnnData<br/>+ control cells] --> B
    D[Test CSV template<br/>target_gene, n_cells] --> B
    E[Perturbation embeddings<br/>drug_dose_embed.pt /<br/>ESM2_pert_features.pt] --> F
    B --> F[inference loop<br/>sample ctrl cells + tile pert embedding]
    F --> G[adata_pred<br/>predicted AnnData]
    G --> H[compute_metrics<br/>cell-eval registry]
    C --> H
```

**Stage 1 — Initialization.** The constructor performs three preparations. It loads a CSV template whose required columns are `target_gene` and `n_cells`, defining which perturbations to generate and at what cell counts. It loads the pretrained model through `from_pretrained` (dispatched to `DeSCOPEForRNA` or `DeSCOPEForATAC` by the subclass). Finally, it splits the input AnnData into `adata_ctrl` (cells matching the control label — `"control"` for ATAC, `"non-targeting"`/`"control_0.0"` for RNA) and `adata_test_ground_truth`; if the AnnData lacks some test perturbations, ground truth registration is skipped with a warning, deferring to manual provision at metric time.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L199-L241), [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L250-L266), [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L268-L284)

**Stage 2 — Generation.** The `inference()` method is the zero-shot engine. For each row of the template, it repeatedly samples control-cell batches uniformly at random (seeded for reproducibility), tiles the target perturbation's embedding across the batch, and calls `model.inference(...)` under `torch.no_grad()` to obtain predicted expression logits. Batches containing NaN are discarded wholesale and resampled; generation continues until the requested `n_cells` is met, with the final batch truncated. Notably, the model conditions *only* on the perturbation embedding — meaning prediction of an unseen drug or gene depends entirely on that embedding being present in the embedding file passed via `gene_embs_file`.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L286-L348)

**Stage 3 — Evaluation.** Results are assembled into `adata_pred`, with one deliberate substitution: generated control cells are discarded and replaced by *real* control cells (`use_generated_control_cells` is asserted `False` and marked as unstable for internal debugging only). Metrics are then computed through `CellEvalMixin.compute_metrics`, which routes to the cell-eval `MetricsEvaluator` with DeSCOPE's built-in format validation bypassed (predictions may contain negative or un-normalized values), plus four extra metrics (`pearson`, `pearson_delta_on_topk_de`, `direction_match_on_topk_de`, `edistance`). Metric selection in the Sci-Plex3 zero-shot notebook spans 21 built-in metrics from `pearson_delta` to `pr_auc`/`roc_auc`, computed on a filtered set of reliably predicted genes.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L160-L196), [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L91-L97), [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L350-L370), [2_inference.ipynb](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/zero-shot/2_inference.ipynb#L100-L120)

> [!TIP]
> The zero-shot workflow's only "leakage surface" is the embedding file. Since `load_gene_embs` restricts embeddings to `self.test_genes` derived from the CSV template, generalization to an unseen perturbation requires that perturbation's embedding (ESM2 for genes, drug-dose vectors for drugs) to exist in the `.pt` file — no model retraining compensates for a missing embedding.

## The Fine-Tuning Workflow: Continued Training on Target Data

Fine-tuning reuses the full training stack — [Trainer and Accelerate Integration](15-trainer-and-accelerate-integration), [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition), [Checkpointing, Resuming, Early Stopping](17-checkpointing-resuming-early-stopping) — with weights seeded from a pretrained checkpoint instead of random initialization. The canonical demonstration is the Sci-Plex3 fine-tuning directory under `tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/fine-tune/`, where the Tahoe-100M pretrained model `descope-tahoe100m-12059-hvgs` adapts to drug perturbation prediction.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[--pretrained_model_name_or_path<br/>= ./descope-tahoe100m-12059-hvgs] --> B{is None?}
    B -- yes --> C[DeSCOPEConfig from model_args<br/>DeSCOPEForRNA config = random init]
    B -- no --> D[DeSCOPEForRNA.from_pretrained<br/>+ alpha_mse_loss, alpha_kl_loss]
    C --> E[DeSCOPETrainer.train]
    D --> E
    F[HFDatasetForRNA<br/>sciplex3_train tokenized] --> E
    E --> G[epoch_X / last_model<br/>checkpoints in output_dir]
    G --> H[InferenceForRNA on<br/>last_model + cell-eval]
```

Three properties of this workflow deserve precision:

**Loss weights transfer at load time.** `from_pretrained` accepts `alpha_mse_loss` and `alpha_kl_loss` as constructor overrides, so the ELBO weighting is a fine-tuning hyperparameter adjustable independently of the checkpoint's original training configuration.

**Fine-tuning is not resuming.** The trainer supports `resume_from_checkpoint`, which calls `accelerator.load_state` to restore optimizer, scheduler, and RNG state, and reconstructs `starting_epoch` from the `epoch_X`/`step_X` directory name. Fine-tuning via `pretrained_model_name_or_path` restores *model weights only* — the optimizer and LR schedule start fresh, and training begins at epoch 0 with a full `num_train_epochs` budget. These are intentionally different mechanisms for different intents.

**The checkpoint contract.** The trainer always writes the final model to `output_dir/last_model`, and periodic checkpoints to `epoch_X/model` (e.g. `--checkpointing_steps=epoch-10`). Both `train_descope.sh` scripts in the ATAC/RNA gene tutorials and the LOO stage-2 script reference `last_model` as the handoff artifact — the same directory that `InferenceForATAC` consumes as `pretrained_model_name_or_path` in `test.ipynb`.

Sources: [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/fine-tune/train_descope.sh#L8-L58), [2_train.py](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/fine-tune/2_train.py#L75-L91), [trainer.py](/src/descope/trainer.py#L67-L96), [trainer.py](/src/descope/trainer.py#L199-L200), [test.ipynb](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/test.ipynb#L29-L35)

## The DeSCOPE_LOO Two-Stage Protocol

The gene-perturbation tutorials encode a more rigorous variant of fine-tuning: **pretrain-then-fine-tune** within a leave-one-out (LOO) evaluation design. `train_descope_loo.sh` chains two complete training runs in one script:

1. **Stage 1 — Pretraining** on a tokenized dataset named `loo_GM12878`: the dataset *excludes* the held-out target perturbation, producing a checkpoint at `$pretrain_output_dir/last_model`.
2. **Stage 2 — Fine-tuning** with `--pretrained_model_name_or_path="$pretrain_output_dir/last_model"` on the full `GM12878` dataset.

Both stages use identical hyperparameters (20 epochs, lr 1e-4 cosine schedule, bf16, batch 64). The distinction is purely in the data split and the checkpoint handoff. This separates *perturbation-generalization* capacity (stage 1, zero knowledge of the held-out target) from *in-distribution adaptation* capacity (stage 2), and pairs with the [Leave-One-Out Evaluation Protocol](21-leave-one-out-evaluation-protocol) described in the dedicated page.

Sources: [train_descope_loo.sh](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train_descope_loo.sh#L3-L9), [train_descope_loo.sh](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train_descope_loo.sh#L56-L98)

## Workflow Comparison

DeSCOPE ships four operational configurations for producing evaluation-ready checkpoints. All converge on the same inference/evaluation entry point:

| Workflow | Entry artifact | `pretrained_model_name_or_path` source | Training involved | Primary use case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Zero-shot** | `InferenceForRNA`/`InferenceForATAC` | Released checkpoint (e.g. `descope-tahoe100m-12059-hvgs`) | None | Assessing generalization to unseen drugs/perturbations |
| **Standard training** | `train.py` + `train_descope.sh` | `None` (random init) | From scratch, 20 epochs | Single cell-line / single-dataset modeling |
| **LOO fine-tuning** | `train_descope_loo.sh` (2 stages) | Stage-1 `last_model` | Pretrain (LOO split) → fine-tune (full data) | Controlled held-out-perturbation evaluation |
| **Drug case fine-tuning** | `2_train.py` + `train_descope.sh` | Tahoe-100M release checkpoints (2k / 5k / 12059 HVGs) | Fine-tune on Sci-Plex3 | Cross-dataset adaptation to drug perturbation |

The three Tahoe-100M checkpoints differ only in gene vocabulary size (each paired with its `merged_*_hvgs.pkl` vocabulary file), trading model capacity and gene coverage against computational cost; the 12059-HVG variant covers 482 of Sci-Plex3's 2,000 genes, and its zero-shot metrics are computed on exactly those genes. The repository's own performance figure compares the zero-shot checkpoint against fine-tuned variants on Sci-Plex3:

![scrna_drug_perturbation_performance](https://github.com/Peg-Wu/DeSCOPE/blob/main/tutorials/RNA_Drug/scrna_drug_perturbation_performance.png?raw=true)

One documented behavior when interpreting these comparisons: the `DeSCOPE_Pretrain_12059_HVGs (zero-shot)` variant shows notably high DE overlap, which the tutorial attributes to a general trend where **DE overlap on the validation set typically declines continuously during training** — a caution against assuming fine-tuning strictly dominates zero-shot on every metric.

Sources: [RNA_Drug README](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/README.md#L15-L23), [RNA_Drug README](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/README.md#L29-L39), [sciplex3_evaluation README](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/README.md#L1), [train_descope.sh](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/fine-tune/train_descope.sh#L6-L8)

## Choosing a Path and Instrumenting It

For intermediate users, the decision logic compresses to data availability and evaluation intent:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q1{Do you have training data<br/>for the target condition?}
    Q1 -- no --> Z[Zero-shot:<br/>released checkpoint + embeddings]
    Q1 -- yes --> Q2{Evaluating generalization<br/>to a held-out perturbation?}
    Q2 -- yes --> LOO[DeSCOPE_LOO:<br/>pretrain on LOO split → fine-tune on full]
    Q2 -- no --> Q3{Large-scale pretrained<br/>checkpoint available?}
    Q3 -- yes --> FT[Fine-tune:<br/>--pretrained_model_name_or_path]
    Q3 -- no --> SCRATCH[Standard training from scratch]
    Z --> EVAL[InferenceForRNA/ATAC<br/>+ compute_metrics]
    FT --> EVAL
    SCRATCH --> EVAL
    LOO --> EVAL
```

Regardless of path, the terminal step is identical: instantiate `InferenceForRNA` or `InferenceForATAC` with the checkpoint directory, a test CSV template, control-cell-bearing AnnData, and the perturbation embedding file; run `infer.inference(...)`; then score with `infer.compute_metrics(...)`. The modality subclasses differ in preprocessing only — ATAC extracts the top-k cCREs from `model.config.input_length` via the EpiAgent-consistent preprocessing, while RNA applies library-size normalization to `target_sum` with an optional raw-counts check.

> [!TIP]
> Keep `skip_raw_counts_check=False` when your AnnData is already log-normalized (as the Sci-Plex3 notebook notes, "Avoid doing log-normalization twice"), and set it to `True` only when feeding raw counts. This flag, modality-specific to `InferenceForRNA`, is the single most common source of silently wrong zero-shot metrics.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/descope/inference.py#L381-L424), [2_inference.ipynb](/tutorials/RNA_Drug/sciplex3_evaluation/zero-shot/2_inference.ipynb#L29-L69), [test.ipynb](/tutorials/ATAC_Gene/test.ipynb#L95-L117)

## Next Steps

- To understand the generation loop and modality preprocessing internals behind the zero-shot path, continue to [Inference Pipeline Design](19-inference-pipeline-design) and the metric definitions in [Perturbation Metrics via Cell-Eval](20-perturbation-metrics-via-cell-eval).
- For the experimental design rationale behind the LOO protocol used in `train_descope_loo.sh`, see [Leave-One-Out Evaluation Protocol](21-leave-one-out-evaluation-protocol).
- To build the tokenized inputs and perturbation embedding files consumed by both workflows, start from [Tutorial Pipeline: Tokenize, Train, Evaluate](4-tutorial-pipeline-tokenize-train-evaluate) and the drug-specific walkthrough in [Drug Perturbation Case Studies: Sciplex3, Tahoe-100M](5-drug-perturbation-case-studies-sciplex3-tahoe-100m).
- For the training mechanics (optimizer, scheduling, distributed execution) shared by standard training and fine-tuning, refer to [Trainer and Accelerate Integration](15-trainer-and-accelerate-integration) and [Distributed Training with DeepSpeed](18-distributed-training-with-deepspeed).

# API Reference and Module Layout



This page is the cartographic entry point to DeSCOPE's codebase: it maps every module in the `descope` package, documents the curated public API surface, and explains how the Sphinx documentation pipeline mirrors that structure. It is deliberately an orientation layer — architectural mechanics (VAE internals, ELBO composition, distributed training) are treated in their own Deep Dive pages, and this page signposts those instead of duplicating them. All claims below are verified directly against source; line references are provided per paragraph.

## Package Architecture at a Glance

DeSCOPE uses a standard `src` layout: all importable code lives under `src/descope/`, and Hatchling is configured to package exactly that directory (`packages = ["src/descope"]`) — meaning there is no namespace trickery, and the distribution name (`descopex`) differs intentionally from the import name (`descope`) [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L5-L10). The package is flat at the top level — seven sibling modules plus one `models/` subpackage — with dependencies flowing strictly downward: `utils` is the shared foundation, `tokenizer` depends on it, `dataset` depends on both, and `inference` composes `utils` with the model classes [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L12-L17), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L21-L30). External scientific dependencies enter only through two channels: `wppkg` (the in-house training/CLI toolkit) into `trainer` and `arguments`, and `cell-eval`/`pdex` into `inference` and `utils` [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L7-L8), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L16-L19).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph descope package
        INIT["__init__.py<br/>public API hub"]
        LOG["logging"]
        UTILS["utils<br/>(foundation)"]
        TOKENIZER["tokenizer"]
        DATASET["dataset"]
        ARGS["arguments"]
        TRAINER["trainer"]
        INFERENCE["inference"]
        subgraph models/
            CONFIG["configuration_descope"]
            MODELING["modeling_descope"]
            MUTILS["models.utils"]
            BASELINES["baselines"]
        end
    end
    TOKENIZER --> UTILS
    DATASET --> TOKENIZER
    DATASET --> UTILS
    INFERENCE --> UTILS
    INFERENCE --> MODELING
    MODELING --> CONFIG
    MODELING --> MUTILS
    ARGS -.->|wppkg.dl.TrainingArguments| WPPKG["wppkg (external)"]
    TRAINER -.->|Trainer, get_logger| WPPKG
    UTILS -.->|cell-eval · pdex| EXT["cell-eval / pdex (external)"]
    INIT --> LOG & TOKENIZER & DATASET & ARGS & TRAINER & INFERENCE & MODELING & BASELINES & UTILS
```

The abbreviated tree below shows each module's role at a glance; the sections that follow document each layer's public surface:

```
src/descope/
├── __init__.py        # version + curated public API hub (71 lines)
├── arguments.py       # three dataclasses for CLI/config (85 lines)
├── dataset.py         # torch Dataset lineages: legacy + HF-backed (335 lines)
├── inference.py       # evaluation mixin + inference engine (424 lines)
├── logging.py         # rank-aware library logger (144 lines)
├── tokenizer.py       # AnnData → HuggingFace Dataset (631 lines)
├── trainer.py         # DeSCOPETrainer over wppkg (227 lines)
├── utils.py           # preprocessing, alignment, metrics (1019 lines)
└── models/            # config, cVAE models, outputs, baselines
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L10), [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L1-L71), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L12-L17), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L16-L30)

## The Public API Surface: What `import descope` Gives You

The package root is a **hand-curated re-export hub**, not a bare `from . import *`: every public symbol is listed explicitly, grouped by subsystem in a fixed order — logging, models, dataset, arguments, tokenizer, inference, trainer, utils [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L1-L36). This means `import descope` pulls the full stack into memory (PyTorch, scanpy, transformers via transitive imports), and it also guarantees a stable namespace: `descope.DeSCOPETrainer` and `descope.tokenizer.TokenizerForRNA` resolve to the same object, so downstream code can use either import style interchangeably. The root also pins `__version__ = "1.0.0"` and provides a `welcome()` banner printer with contact information, which is the only function defined (not re-exported) at the root [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L39-L71).

> [!TIP]
> **Import side effect**: line 8 of `__init__.py` calls `set_verbosity_info()` at module import time — the moment any script does `import descope`, the library's root logger verbosity is globally reset to INFO, overriding any prior logging customization. If you need custom logging, configure it *after* importing descope, or use `descope.logging.get_logger` for an independent logger that ignores this default [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L8), [src/descope/logging.py](src/descope/logging.py#L66-L89).

The full top-level export inventory:

| Subsystem | Symbols exported at root |
|---|---|
| Logging | `set_verbosity_info`, `set_verbosity_warning` |
| Models | `DeSCOPEConfig`, `DeSCOPEForATAC`, `DeSCOPEForRNA`, `mean_baseline` |
| Datasets | `HFDatasetForATAC`, `HFDatasetForRNA` |
| Arguments | `DeSCOPEDataArguments`, `DeSCOPEModelArguments`, `DeSCOPETrainingArguments` |
| Tokenizer | `TokenizerForATAC`, `TokenizerForRNA`, `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_atac`, `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_rna` |
| Inference | `InferenceForATAC`, `InferenceForRNA` |
| Trainer | `DeSCOPETrainer` |
| Utils | `UniformFeatureForAnnData`, `intersect_adatas_for_celltype_transfer`, `load_gene_names_engine`, `load_gene_embs`, `preprocess_atac_perturbation_adata_consistent_with_epiagent`, `preprocess_rna_perturbation_adata`, `pearson_delta_on_topk_de`, `direction_match_on_topk_de`, `pearson`, `edistance`, `build_de` |

Sources: [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L1-L36), [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L39-L71), [src/descope/logging.py](src/descope/logging.py#L66-L89)

## Data Preparation Layer: `tokenizer` and `dataset`

The `descope.tokenizer` module owns the AnnData → HuggingFace conversion. Its core primitive is `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset`, which converts cells into a three-column Dataset (`labels`, `pert_gene`, `celltype`) in memory-bounded chunks (`chunk_size=20000` default) [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L58-L143). On top of it sit two modality-specific entry points that each run preprocessing then filtering then tokenization: `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_atac` (top-k cCRE selection at 50,000 by default) and `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_rna` (CPM-like normalization with `target_sum=1e4`), both saving to disk via `save_to_disk` [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L146-L222), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L225-L305). The `TokenizerForATAC` / `TokenizerForRNA` classes wrap this machinery for **multi-cell-line pretraining**: they are initialized with a *finetune* cell line whose feature list and perturbation gene list become the contract, and their `tokenize()` method iterates over lists of *pretrain* cell lines, aligning each to that contract [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L308-L435), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L438-L631). The only private names are `_filter_perturbations` (include/exclude filtering that always preserves the control condition) and `_merge_list_of_dicts`; both are excluded from the rendered docs [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L19-L55), [docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst](docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst#L8-L10).

`descope.dataset` contains **two parallel lineages**, and the module's own comments label them: the `# Slow | Deprecated` family — abstract `BaseDataset` (torch `Dataset` + ABC) with concrete `DatasetForATAC`/`DatasetForRNA` — and the `# Fast` family — `HFBaseDataset`, which wraps an already-tokenized `datasets.Dataset` instead of a raw AnnData object [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L22-L23), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L174-L178). The HF family enforces its contract at construction time: `_check_hf_dataset_features` raises `ValueError` unless the dataset carries exactly `labels`, `pert_gene`, and `celltype` columns, and `__init_subclass__` forces every subclass to declare a non-None `MAIN_INPUT_NAME` class attribute [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L180-L189), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L225-L235). `HFBaseDataset` also implements `__getitems__` (plural) for batched fetching, injects `pert_gene_emb` from ESM2 embeddings via `load_gene_embs`, optionally attaches `mse_weights` from a pickle file, and provides a passthrough `collate_fn` [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L207-L214), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L277-L320). The concrete production classes are deliberately trivial — `HFDatasetForATAC` and `HFDatasetForRNA` only set class attributes (`MAIN_INPUT_NAME` = `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` vs `ctrl_cell_expr`) — because all behavior lives in the base [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L323-L334).

| Class | Lineage | Input contract | Batch key (`MAIN_INPUT_NAME`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BaseDataset` → `DatasetForATAC` / `DatasetForRNA` | Slow (deprecated) | raw AnnData or `.h5ad` path | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` / `ctrl_cell_expr` |
| `HFBaseDataset` → `HFDatasetForATAC` / `HFDatasetForRNA` | Fast (production) | tokenized `datasets.Dataset` with `labels`, `pert_gene`, `celltype` | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` / `ctrl_cell_expr` |

Sources: [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L58-L143), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L146-L305), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L308-L631), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L174-L235), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L277-L334), [docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst](docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst#L1-L10)

## Model Layer: the `models` Subpackage

The `models` subpackage is where the cVAE lives, structured exactly as HuggingFace convention dictates. `configuration_descope.py` defines a single `DeSCOPEConfig(PretrainedConfig)` with `model_type = "descope"` and defaults that define the reference architecture: `hidden_size=672`, `input_pert_gene_embedding_size=5120` (the ESM2 embedding width), and `input_length=18080` (the shared RNA/ATAC feature dimension) [src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28). `modeling_descope.py` builds the network from four components — `PertGeneEncoder` (projects ESM2 embeddings to hidden size), `VariationalEncoder` (emits mean/logvar chunks and performs reparameterization), `VariationalDecoder` (reconstructs `input_length` outputs) — composed into `DeSCOPEPretrainedModel(PreTrainedModel)` and then the two concrete heads, `DeSCOPEForATAC` and `DeSCOPEForRNA` [src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L15-L130). A source comment makes the design intent explicit: the RNA and ATAC models are architecturally identical but are kept as **two distinct classes** so each modality can evolve independently [src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L118). Supporting files complete the layer: `models/utils.py` holds the typed model outputs (`DeSCOPEForATACOutput`/`DeSCOPEForRNAOutput`, each carrying `loss`, `mse_loss`, `kl_loss`, `logits`), the closed-form `kl_loss_func`, and an auxiliary `ZINBLoss`; `baselines.py` provides the `mean_baseline` function with its `MeanBaselineType` enum (`perturbed_mean` / `matching_mean`), implementing published baseline predictors for benchmarking [src/descope/models/utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L12-L44), [src/descope/models/baselines.py](src/descope/models/baselines.py#L12-L27).

Notably, `DeSCOPEModelArguments` in `arguments.py` mirrors `DeSCOPEConfig` field-for-field with identical defaults (`hidden_act="gelu"`, `hidden_size=672`, `hidden_dropout=0`, `pert_gene_encoder_layers=1`, `variational_encoder_layers=4`, `variational_decoder_layers=4`) — the dataclass is the CLI-facing twin of the config object, so the two must be kept in sync when adding hyperparameters [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L49-L80), [src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L6-L28). For the mathematical and architectural treatment of these components, see [Conditional VAE Architecture Overview](6-conditional-vae-architecture-overview) and [Model Configuration Reference](7-model-configuration-reference); this page intentionally stops at the API boundary.

| Class | Base class | File | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeSCOPEConfig` | `PretrainedConfig` | configuration_descope.py | Serialization-ready hyperparameter container |
| `PertGeneEncoder` | `nn.Module` | modeling_descope.py | ESM2 embedding → hidden space |
| `VariationalEncoder` | `nn.Module` | modeling_descope.py | Mean/logvar heads + reparameterization |
| `VariationalDecoder` | `nn.Module` | modeling_descope.py | Latent → `input_length` reconstruction |
| `DeSCOPEPretrainedModel` | `PreTrainedModel` | modeling_descope.py | Shared base; enables `from_pretrained` |
| `DeSCOPEForATAC` / `DeSCOPEForRNA` | `DeSCOPEPretrainedModel` | modeling_descope.py | Concrete models (identical architecture) |
| `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` / `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` | `ModelOutput` dataclass | models/utils.py | Typed forward outputs |
| `mean_baseline` | function | baselines.py | Mean-predictor baselines for benchmarking |

Sources: [src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L4-L28), [src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L15-L130), [src/descope/models/utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L12-L44), [src/descope/models/baselines.py](src/descope/models/baselines.py#L12-L27), [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L49-L80)

## Training Layer: `trainer` and `arguments`

`DeSCOPETrainer` extends the `Trainer` from the external `wppkg` library, inheriting the accelerate-based training loop, and the module makes one unusual move at import time: it **monkey-patches** `Trainer._init_logger` (line 32) so every Trainer instance writes per-run log files into `args.output_dir/run.log` with console output silenced except on the main process [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L11-L32). The subclass adds forward-signature introspection — `self.model_forward_keys` is derived from the unwrapped model's `forward` parameters, which is how the Trainer decides which batch dict keys to pass through under accelerate wrapping — plus explicit resume-from-checkpoint logic that parses `epoch_*` / `step_*` checkpoint directory names [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L44-L96). Its class docstring states three operational constraints you should treat as contract: early stopping does not survive resume; `eval_every_n_epochs` must align with `checkpointing_steps` because the best model is not auto-saved; and the final model is always saved even when early stopping fires [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L36-L43). Loss bookkeeping uses an `Accumulator` named over `loss`, `mse_loss`, `kl_loss` — the three quantities defined by the model outputs in `models/utils.py` [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L98).

The `descope.arguments` module defines the three dataclasses that parameterize a run, all configured as `field()`-based dataclasses with `metadata={"help": ...}` strings for CLI generation [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L1-L4). `DeSCOPETrainingArguments` extends `wppkg.dl.TrainingArguments` (inheriting the standard accelerate argument set) and adds exactly three fields: the ELBO weights `alpha_mse_loss` and `alpha_kl_loss`, and `pretrained_model_name_or_path` for finetuning checkpoints [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L6-L22). `DeSCOPEDataArguments` points training at tokenized data with `tokenized_datasets_dir`, `keep_in_memory`, `ctrl_name`, and `gene_embs_file`; `DeSCOPEModelArguments` carries the architecture hyperparameters discussed above [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L25-L46). The full ELBO semantics of `alpha_mse_loss`/`alpha_kl_loss` are covered in [ELBO Loss: MSE and KL Composition](16-elbo-loss-mse-and-kl-composition), and checkpoint/resume behavior in [Checkpointing, Resuming, Early Stopping](17-checkpointing-resuming-early-stopping).

| Dataclass | Inherits | Added fields (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `DeSCOPETrainingArguments` | `wppkg.dl.TrainingArguments` | `alpha_mse_loss=1.0`, `alpha_kl_loss=1.0`, `pretrained_model_name_or_path=None` |
| `DeSCOPEDataArguments` | (none) | `tokenized_datasets_dir="./tokenized_dataset/K562"`, `keep_in_memory=False`, `ctrl_name="control"`, `gene_embs_file="./ESM2_pert_features.pt"` |
| `DeSCOPEModelArguments` | (none) | `hidden_act="gelu"`, `hidden_size=672`, `hidden_dropout=0`, `pert_gene_encoder_layers=1`, `variational_encoder_layers=4`, `variational_decoder_layers=4`, … |

Sources: [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L11-L43), [src/descope/trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L44-L98), [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L1-L46), [src/descope/arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L49-L80)

## Inference and Evaluation Layer: `inference`

`descope.inference` is built on a **mixin + template-method** composition. `CellEvalMixin` bridges to the external `cell-eval` package: it exposes `all_metrics` / `all_de_metrics` / `all_anndata_pair_metrics` properties that read the cell-eval metrics registry live, and its own `extra_metrics_func` dict (`pearson`, `pearson_delta_on_topk_de`, `direction_match_on_topk_de`, `edistance`) exposed as an attribute-style `edict` [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L70-L116). Its `compute_metrics` method wraps cell-eval's `MetricsEvaluator` and deliberately disables cell-eval's default format validation, because DeSCOPE models can emit raw-scale or negative predictions that would fail a log1p check [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L160-L196). `BaseInference(CellEvalMixin, ABC)` is the engine: it consumes a test CSV template with required columns `target_gene` and `n_cells`, splits input AnnData into control and ground-truth subsets, then `inference()` generates predictions batch-by-batch by sampling control cells, attaching the target gene's ESM2 embedding, and discarding any batch containing NaN logits until the requested cell count is met [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L199-L284), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L286-L348). `_organize_final_results` performs a subtle correction — generated "control" predictions are **discarded and replaced with real control cells** before assembly into the predicted AnnData [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L350-L370). The concrete subclasses are again minimal: `InferenceForATAC` fixes ATAC preprocessing and `DeSCOPEForATAC.from_pretrained`; `InferenceForRNA` adds `target_sum`/`skip_raw_counts_check` knobs and wires `DeSCOPEForRNA.from_pretrained` [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L381-L424).

> [!TIP]
> **Metric-scale warning**: `compute_metrics` patches `cell_eval._evaluator._build_anndata_pair` at line 183 to skip log1p/normalization validation entirely (the strict variant remains available as `_compute_metrics`). If you compare DeSCOPE results against other tools, confirm all parties evaluate on the same value scale — this bypass exists precisely because DeSCOPE's softplus-free raw outputs may include negatives [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L160-L196).

Evaluation methodology — how these metrics are orchestrated, and the leave-one-out protocol built on them — is documented in [Inference Pipeline Design](19-inference-pipeline-design), [Perturbation Metrics via Cell-Eval](20-perturbation-metrics-via-cell-eval), and [Leave-One-Out Evaluation Protocol](21-leave-one-out-evaluation-protocol).

Sources: [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L70-L196), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L199-L348), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L350-L424)

## Utility and Logging Layer

`descope.utils` is the largest module (1,019 lines) and serves two audiences. As infrastructure, it holds the shared preprocessing primitives that the tokenizer, datasets, and inference modules all import — `preprocess_rna_perturbation_adata`, `preprocess_atac_perturbation_adata_consistent_with_epiagent`, `load_gene_embs` — plus the feature-alignment machinery: `UniformFeatureForAnnData`, a callable class that reindexes any AnnData onto a target feature list, zero-padding missing genes and resolving duplicates via the `DuplicatedFeatureHandling` enum (`mean_pooling` or `max_pooling`) [src/descope/utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L25-L116), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L8-L14). As a toolkit, it provides the evaluation metrics (`pearson`, `edistance`, `pearson_delta_on_topk_de`, `direction_match_on_topk_de`, `build_de`) and data-joining helpers (`intersect_adatas_for_celltype_transfer`, `load_gene_names_engine`) that `inference.py` consumes through `CellEvalMixin` [src/descope/utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L14-L22), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L21-L29). Feature alignment semantics belong to [Feature Alignment and Vocabulary Handling](14-feature-alignment-and-vocabulary-handling); this page records only the API positions.

`descope.logging` is a self-contained, dependency-free module implementing a HuggingFace-style verbosity API. The private `_configure_logger` centralizes handler wiring with **rank-aware levels** — on non-main processes (`local_rank` not in `[-1, 0]`) console output drops to WARN, and file handlers are only attached on rank 0, which prevents duplicate log lines under distributed training [src/descope/logging.py](src/descope/logging.py#L5-L40). Public entry points are `setup_root_logger` and `get_logger` (the latter creates a non-propagating independent logger), plus the `set_verbosity_*` shortcut family spanning DEBUG through CRITICAL, each funneling into `set_verbosity` [src/descope/logging.py](src/descope/logging.py#L43-L144).

Sources: [src/descope/utils.py](src/descope/utils.py#L1-L120), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L8-L14), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L21-L29), [src/descope/logging.py](src/descope/logging.py#L5-L40), [src/descope/logging.py](src/descope/logging.py#L43-L144)

## The ATAC/RNA Naming Symmetry

The single most important pattern for navigating this API is the **five-fold ATAC/RNA symmetry**: every functional layer offers exactly one class per modality under parallel naming, and pairing is positional rather than incidental. Each pair shares its base implementation and differs only in modality constants — notably the batch dictionary key (`ctrl_cell_tf_idf` for ATAC vs `ctrl_cell_expr` for RNA) and the obs-column/control-label defaults (`perturbation`/`control` vs `gene`/`non-targeting`) [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L111-L141), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L381-L413). When reading any Deep Dive page, you can mentally substitute the other modality's counterpart and remain correct — the exception being preprocessing details, which genuinely differ and are covered in [Perturbation Filtering and Preprocessing](13-perturbation-filtering-and-preprocessing).

| Layer | ATAC variant | RNA variant | Distinguishing defaults |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer (batch) | `TokenizerForATAC` | `TokenizerForRNA` | `topk_ccres=50000` vs `target_sum=1e4` |
| Tokenize (single cell line) | `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_atac` | `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_rna` | `pert_col="perturbation"` vs `pert_col="gene"` |
| Dataset | `HFDatasetForATAC` | `HFDatasetForRNA` | `MAIN_INPUT_NAME="ctrl_cell_tf_idf"` vs `"ctrl_cell_expr"` |
| Model | `DeSCOPEForATAC` | `DeSCOPEForRNA` | Identical architecture, separate checkpoints |
| Inference | `InferenceForATAC` | `InferenceForRNA` | `ctrl_name="control"` vs `"non-targeting"` |

Sources: [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L110-L141), [src/descope/dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L323-L334), [src/descope/inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L381-L424), [src/descope/tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L146-L237)

## Sphinx Autodoc Layout

The published API docs are generated from `docs/source/`, and their structure encodes an editorial decision. `API.rst` is a pure aggregator: seven sections (Tokenizer, Dataset, Trainer, Inference, Utils, Logging, Arguments), each a one-file toctree pointing at a matching `descope.<module>.rst` [docs/source/API.rst](docs/source/API.rst#L1-L58). Each leaf file follows an identical autodoc recipe — `automodule` with `:members:`, `:undoc-members:`, `:show-inheritance:` — so the rendered docs are exhaustive for documented and undocumented public members alike, while `:exclude-members:` strips the private helpers that violate the abstraction boundary (verified: `_filter_perturbations`, `_merge_list_of_dicts` in the tokenizer page) [docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst](docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst#L1-L10). Conspicuously, **there is no `descope.models` entry** in the API toctree — the model layer is instead documented narratively in the Deep Dive section of this catalog, keeping generated reference output focused on the usage-facing modules [docs/source/API.rst](docs/source/API.rst#L1-L58), [docs/source/index.rst](docs/source/index.rst#L6-L16). The rendered pages sit in a site-wide toctree ordered Installation → Datasets → Tutorials → API → Acknowledgements, making API the reference anchor after the tutorial material [docs/source/index.rst](docs/source/index.rst#L9-L16).

| Documentation file | Automodule target | Exclusions |
|---|---|---|
| `descope.tokenizer.rst` | `descope.tokenizer` | `_filter_perturbations`, `_merge_list_of_dicts` |
| `descope.dataset.rst` | `descope.dataset` | (same recipe) |
| `descope.trainer.rst` | `descope.trainer` | (same recipe) |
| `descope.inference.rst` | `descope.inference` | (same recipe) |
| `descope.utils.rst` | `descope.utils` | (same recipe) |
| `descope.logging.rst` | `descope.logging` | (same recipe) |
| `descope.arguments.rst` | `descope.arguments` | (same recipe) |

Sources: [docs/source/API.rst](docs/source/API.rst#L1-L58), [docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst](docs/source/descope.tokenizer.rst#L1-L10), [docs/source/index.rst](docs/source/index.rst#L1-L16)

## Package Metadata and Dependencies

`pyproject.toml` pins the contract that makes this layout installable and reproducible. The build uses Hatchling; the distribution is `descopex` at version 1.0.0 (matching `descope.__version__`), MIT-licensed, and requires Python ≥ 3.10 [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L19). The dependency list is short and telling: `torch` (with deepspeed deliberately commented as optional, referencing README install instructions), the in-house `wppkg==0.1.4`, evaluation stack `cell-eval==0.6.6` (with the note that 0.6.6 was the experimentally validated version), and `pdex==0.1.28` for parallel differential expression [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L20-L26). Note what is *not* pinned — `scanpy`, `transformers`, `datasets`, `accelerate` — these arrive transitively through `wppkg` and `cell-eval`, so reproducibility depends on the pinned intermediaries resolving consistent versions. The three exact pins correspond precisely to the three integration seams identified in the dependency graph: training loop (`wppkg`), metrics (`cell-eval`), and DE computation (`pdex`) [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L20-L26).

| Property | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Distribution / import name | `descopex` / `descope` | Deliberate divergence |
| Version | 1.0.0 | Mirrored in `src/descope/__init__.py` |
| Build backend | Hatchling | `packages = ["src/descope"]` |
| Python | ≥ 3.10 | Modern typing syntax (`list[str]`) used throughout |
| Hard pins | `wppkg==0.1.4`, `cell-eval==0.6.6`, `pdex==0.1.28` | Version-sensitive integrations |
| Optional | `deepspeed` | Commented out; see README |

Sources: [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L36), [src/descope/__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L1)

## Extending and Navigating from Here

For the working developer, the practical reading order through this codebase follows the dependency graph bottom-up: `utils` (alignment + metrics primitives) → `tokenizer` (dataset contracts) → `dataset` (batch semantics) → `models` (forward signatures) → `trainer` → `inference`. The Deep Dive catalog mirrors this exactly, so after this overview, continue with the layer that matches your current task: data work starts at [Tokenization: AnnData to HuggingFace Datasets](12-tokenization-anndata-to-huggingface-datasets), training work at [Trainer and Accelerate Integration](15-trainer-and-accelerate-integration), evaluation work at [Inference Pipeline Design](19-inference-pipeline-design), and model internals at [Conditional VAE Architecture Overview](6-conditional-vae-architecture-overview). If your goal is to add a new modality beyond ATAC and RNA, the final page — [Extending DeSCOPE to New Modalities](24-extending-descope-to-new-modalities) — walks the concrete steps, and the symmetry table above tells you exactly which five classes you will need to parallel.


# Extending DeSCOPE to New Modalities



DeSCOPE ships with two first-class modalities — scRNA-seq (`DeSCOPEForRNA`) and scATAC-seq (`DeSCOPEForATAC`) — but the framework was deliberately structured so that a third, fourth, or Nth modality (spatial transcriptomics, CITE-seq protein counts, methylation arrays) requires **no changes to the training or evaluation core**. This page is the authoritative guide for advanced developers: it documents the extension doctrine extracted from the codebase, the five enforced contracts your new modality must satisfy, and a step-by-step implementation workflow with verified code anchors.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L118), [__init__.py](src/descope/__init__.py#L13-L26)

## The Modality Extension Doctrine

The codebase states its own extension philosophy in a NOTE that precedes both model classes: *"The RNA and ATAC models have identical architectures; we maintain them as two distinct models to support independent adjustment for each data modality."* This is the governing principle. Rather than building a single config-switched model, DeSCOPE maintains a **parallel class triple per modality** — Tokenizer, HFDataset, Model, plus a fourth surface for Inference — while keeping every mechanism that operates *across* modalities (trainer, control-cell pairing, ELBO machinery, metrics) in shared base classes. The two tutorial training scripts are line-for-line identical except for the class names they import, which is the strongest evidence that adding a modality is a "fill in the parallel slots" exercise, not a core surgery task.

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L117-L118), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L199-L200), [train.py (ATAC)](tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train.py#L44-L85), [train.py (RNA)](tutorials/RNA_Gene/train.py#L44-L85)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph MOD["Modality-Specific Surfaces — you implement these"]
        TOK["TokenizerFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>modality preprocessing + feature alignment"]
        DS["HFDatasetFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>sets MAIN_INPUT_NAME"]
        MODEL["DeSCOPEFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>implements forward contract"]
        INF["InferenceFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>implements load_model + preprocess_adata"]
    end
    subgraph CORE["Shared Core — you never touch these"]
        CFG["DeSCOPEConfig"]
        BASE["HFBaseDataset<br/>ctrl pairing · gene-embs · mse weights"]
        TR["DeSCOPETrainer<br/>batch filtered by forward signature"]
        EVAL["CellEvalMixin<br/>cell-eval + extra metrics"]
    end
    TOK -- "labels · pert_gene · celltype" --> DS
    DS --> BASE
    BASE -- "batch dict" --> TR
    MODEL --> TR
    TR --> MODEL
    CFG -.->|dims derived from data| MODEL
    INF --> MODEL
    EVAL --> INF
```

### Per-Modality Class Matrix

Each existing modality fills every row of this matrix identically in shape; a new modality adds one more row:

| Extension surface | ATAC slot | RNA slot | Base class / contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer class | `TokenizerForATAC` | `TokenizerForRNA` | ft-set defines canonical features + perturbation set |
| Function tokenizer | `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_atac` | `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset_for_rna` | Emits the 3-column HF schema |
| Model | `DeSCOPEForATAC` | `DeSCOPEForRNA` | Subclass `DeSCOPEPretrainedModel` |
| Model output | `DeSCOPEForATACOutput` | `DeSCOPEForRNAOutput` | `ModelOutput` with `loss/mse_loss/kl_loss/logits` |
| HF Dataset | `HFDatasetForATAC` | `HFDatasetForRNA` | Subclass `HFBaseDataset` + `MAIN_INPUT_NAME` |
| Inference | `InferenceForATAC` | `InferenceForRNA` | Subclass `BaseInference` (ABC) |
| Forward main input kwarg | `ctrl_cell_tf_idf` | `ctrl_cell_expr` | Must match dataset `MAIN_INPUT_NAME` |
| Preprocessing fn | `preprocess_atac_perturbation_adata_consistent_with_epiagent` | `preprocess_rna_perturbation_adata` | AnnData in → model-ready AnnData out |
| Default `ctrl_name` / `pert_col` | `"control"` / `"perturbation"` | `"non-targeting"` / `"gene"` | Conventions, overridable via args |

Sources: [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L119-L196), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L201-L283), [models/utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L12-L25), [dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L324-L334), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L381-L391), [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L308-L435), [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L438-L631)

## The Five Enforced Contracts

DeSCOPE does not rely on convention alone — several contracts are enforced at runtime, which means a new modality either satisfies them or fails fast and loudly. Understanding these is the difference between a clean integration and a mysterious `KeyError` deep in training.

| # | Contract | Enforcement point | Failure mode if violated |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tokenized HF dataset has columns `labels`, `pert_gene`, `celltype` | `HFBaseDataset._check_hf_dataset_features` | `ValueError` listing missing features at dataset construction |
| 2 | Dataset subclass defines non-None `MAIN_INPUT_NAME` | `__init_subclass__` hook on the base class | `NotImplementedError` at class definition time |
| 3 | Batch keys ⊆ model `forward` parameter names | `DeSCOPETrainer.__init__` introspects `forward` signature; train loop filters the batch | Extra keys silently dropped; a missing forward kwarg means it stays `None` — a silent data bug |
| 4 | Model forward returns an output with `loss`, `mse_loss`, `kl_loss` | `DeSCOPETrainer` reads these attributes directly | `AttributeError` in the training loop |
| 5 | Inference subclass implements `load_model` + `preprocess_adata` | `BaseInference` abstract methods | `TypeError` at instantiation |

Sources: [dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L225-L235), [dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L169-L185), [trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L43-L46), [trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L109-L115), [inference.py](src/descope/inference.py#L372-L378)

> [!TIP]
> Contract 3 is the linchpin that decouples modality from the trainer: `DeSCOPETrainer` builds `self.model_forward_keys` from `inspect.signature(unwrapped_model.forward)` and filters every batch to those keys before calling the model. Your `MAIN_INPUT_NAME` string must therefore be *exactly* the first parameter name of your model's `forward` — this is how `HFDatasetForATAC("ctrl_cell_tf_idf")` binds to `DeSCOPEForATAC.forward(ctrl_cell_tf_idf, ...)` and `HFDatasetForRNA("ctrl_cell_expr")` binds to `DeSCOPEForRNA.forward(ctrl_cell_expr, ...)` with zero trainer modifications.

### Contract 1 in Depth: The Three-Column HF Schema

Every modality converges on the same tokenized artifact: a HuggingFace `Dataset` with exactly three columns — `"labels"` (the model-ready feature vector per cell), `"pert_gene"` (the perturbation identity string), and `"celltype"` (the context label used to pair controls). The shared function `tokenize_adata_to_hf_dataset` produces this for both existing modalities, and `_check_hf_dataset_features` rejects anything missing them at load time. This schema is *the* interchange format of the framework: everything downstream (control pairing, embedding lookup, cell-eval export) keys off these names.

Sources: [tokenizer.py](src/descope/tokenizer.py#L58-L124), [dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L225-L235)

### Contract 2 & 3 in Depth: The Name Binding

`HFBaseDataset.__getitems__` constructs the batch by selecting a random control cell per `celltype` for each perturbed cell and stores it under `batch[self.MAIN_INPUT_NAME]` (control cells map to themselves, keeping the VAE's prior path well-defined). Alongside it, the batch carries `pert_gene_emb` (stacked from the embedding file via `load_gene_embs`) and optional `mse_weights`. The trainer then keeps only keys matching your model's forward signature — so `pert_gene`, `celltype`, and other metadata flow through the dataset but never reach the model unless you declare them.

Sources: [dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L277-L313), [dataset.py](src/descope/dataset.py#L202-L205), [trainer.py](src/descope/trainer.py#L109-L112)

## Architecture Is Dimension-Fluid: What the Config Does (and Doesn't) Encode

`DeSCOPEConfig` is deliberately modality-agnostic. It carries only two modality-relevant scalars: `input_length` (the feature-vector width — 18,080 for both existing modalities by default) and `input_pert_gene_embedding_size` (the perturbation-identity embedding width — 5,120 for ESM2). Crucially, `DeSCOPEModelArguments` exposes **no** `input_length` argument at all. Instead, both tutorial scripts derive the full configuration from the dataset itself: `input_length=train_ds[0]["labels"].shape[-1]` and `input_pert_gene_embedding_size=train_ds[0]["pert_gene_emb"].shape[-1]`. The practical consequence for extension work is profound: **your tokenized dataset and embedding file define the architecture**, so the same model code instantiates correctly for any feature count or embedding width without touching the config class.

Sources: [configuration_descope.py](src/descope/models/configuration_descope.py#L1-L28), [arguments.py](src/descope/arguments.py#L10-L85), [train.py (ATAC)](tutorials/ATAC_Gene/train.py#L52-L64)

> [!TIP]
> Because architecture dims are read from `train_ds[0]`, feature alignment in tokenization is not just hygiene — it is what pins the network's input/output width. If your modality has a different natural feature count (say, 5,000 proteins), do not pad to 18,080; simply tokenize to your true width and `input_length` follows. All MLPs are built by the dimension-parameterized `build_mlp`, and the variational encoders take `in_dim` as an explicit constructor argument (`VariationalEncoder(config, in_dim=config.input_length + config.hidden_size)`), so nothing else needs to change.

Sources: [models/utils.py](src/descope/models/utils.py#L104-L133), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L36-L73), [modeling_descope.py](src/descope/models/modeling_descope.py#L128-L130)

## Step-by-Step: Adding a New Modality

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1. Write preprocess fn<br/>raw AnnData → model-ready AnnData<br/>(value space decision lives here)"] --> B["2. Build TokenizerFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>ft set pins canonical features<br/>+ perturbation vocabulary"]
    B --> C["3. Emit HF Dataset<br/>labels · pert_gene · celltype"]
    C --> D["4. Build HFDatasetFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>MAIN_INPUT_NAME = ctrl_cell_&lt;m&gt;"]
    E["5. Prepare perturbation<br/>embedding .pt file"] --> F
    D --> F["6. Build DeSCOPEFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>forward(main_input, pert_gene_emb,<br/>labels?, mse_weights?) → Output"]
    F --> G["7. Build InferenceFor&lt;M&gt;<br/>load_model + preprocess_adata"]
    G --> H["8. Copy tutorial train script<br/>swap class names — done"]
    H --> I{Smoke test:<br/>1 batch forward +<br/>1 inference call}
    I -- pass --> J["Full training + LOO eval"]
    I -- fail --> K["Check name binding<br/>and 3-column schema"]
    K --> D
```

### Step 1 — Preprocessing: Decide the Value Space
